articles.title: PM Shehbaz departs on 4-day visit to China - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif departed on a four-day visit to China from May 23 to 26, accompanied by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, IT Minister Shaza Fatima, and PM’s adviser Tariq Fatemi. The visit marks the 75th anniversary of Pakistan-China diplomatic relations and will focus on strengthening bilateral cooperation in political, economic, and strategic domains.  The premier will meet with President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Qiang, discussing topics such as CPEC development, trade, investment, industrial cooperation, agricultural modernization, information technology, science and technology, and people-to-people exchanges.

articles.title: Elon Musk's SpaceX launches Starship V3 rocket after delays
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX successfully launched its massive Starship V3 rocket on a test flight, marking the largest and most powerful rocket in history. The uncrewed rocket deployed 20 dummy satellites before splashing down in the Indian Ocean after an hour-long journey. Elon Musk, CEO of SpaceX, praised the team's achievement while NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman expressed excitement for future missions to the moon and Mars.  The successful test flight, despite engine failures, is expected to boost confidence for investors and NASA as it prepares for future space endeavors.

articles.title: Centre promised more legislative powers for Ladakh, says delegation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) proposed a new mechanism to grant Ladakh greater legislative, financial, and administrative powers within the existing Union Territory framework.  Civil society members who attended a sub-committee meeting with MHA officials on Friday (May 22, 2026) reported that the talks were positive and that the MHA would soon send a draft outlining the proposed changes.

articles.title: Jana Nayagan leak case: Madras High Court denies bail to six accused - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Madras High Court denied bail to six individuals who shared and watched the leaked film "Jana Nayagan" before its official release.  Justice R. Sakthivel dismissed all bail petitions after the prosecution argued that the illegal viewing of the movie by millions constituted a serious offense.

articles.title: Seven MLAs from Chennai find place in Tamil Nadu cabinet: highest in recent years - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and seven other ministers from Chennai constituencies were sworn in on Thursday, marking a significant representation for the city in the new cabinet.  This is one of the highest contributions to the current cabinet from Chennai, with many top leaders from the Tamil Nadu Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) contesting from the city and becoming ministers.

articles.title: TANUVAS invites applications for UG courses - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu Veterinary and Animal Sciences University (Tanuvas) has opened its application portal for undergraduate courses, including Bachelor's in Veterinary Sciences and Animal Husbandry, and various B. Tech programs. Applications are open from 10 a.m. on May 25 to 5 p.m. on June 17 through the university's website: https://adm.tanuvas.ac.in.  Candidates can find details regarding seat reservations for NRIs, NRI-sponsored candidates, and foreign nationals on the portal.

articles.title: Innovation begins with understanding the fundamentals: Prakash Balasubramanian - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prakash Balasubramanian, senior director at Infineon Technologies, emphasized the importance of foundational knowledge for technological breakthroughs during the inauguration of "Nirmaan Utsav" in Kalaburagi city. He highlighted the evolution of technologies over decades and urged students to think innovatively. Deputy Commissioner of Police (Law and Order) Shaloo encouraged students to combine academic learning with practical experience and stay updated on emerging fields like drones, artificial intelligence, and cybersecurity. HKE Society president and MLC Shashil Namoshi noted that PDA Engineering College is nurturing future-ready students through events like "Nirmaan Utsav."

articles.title: Kevin Warsh sworn in as Fed chair as Trump faces backlash over economy | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kevin Warsh, hand-picked by Donald Trump, was sworn in as chair of the US Federal Reserve, tasked with navigating an uncertain economic outlook.  Warsh faces pressure to cut interest rates despite rising inflation and criticism over his perceived lack of independence from the president.  The new Fed chair pledged a "reform-oriented" approach while acknowledging challenges facing the economy. Public opinion polls show growing dissatisfaction with Trump's economic record, particularly regarding immigration enforcement and affordability issues. The US Federal Reserve faces mounting pressure to address these concerns as Americans grapple with rising fuel prices and inflation.

articles.title: KARD, Khandre condemn assault on BRIMS resident doctor - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka Association of Resident Doctors (KARD) and Bidar district in-charge Minister Eshwar B. Khandre condemned the alleged assault of a resident doctor at Bidar Institute of Medical Sciences (BRIMS), urging the state government to improve security for doctors working in public hospitals.  A letter sent to the Director of Medical Education on Friday stated that Tukaram, a 28-year-old orthopaedic resident doctor, was allegedly assaulted while attending to an injured patient in the casualty ward around 1 a.m. on Friday.

articles.title: US green card applicants will now have to return to home countries to apply, DHS says | US immigration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: USCIS announced a new policy requiring foreigners seeking green cards to apply for them outside the United States. The move, criticized by aid groups and immigration attorneys, will force many applicants to leave the country while their cases are processed, potentially impacting families and creating further strain on an already burdened system.  The agency cited the need to ensure the integrity of the immigration system and prevent loopholes, but the policy change is expected to have significant consequences for those seeking permanent residency in the US.

articles.title: Bengali actors face heat after power shift to BJP; FIR filed over 2021 social media posts linked to post-poll violence - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Parambrata Chatterjee, a Bengali actor, announced he had to align with the Trinamool Congress after the recent West Bengal Assembly election results.  He stated this decision was made for his one-year-old son, prompting strong reactions from social media users and fellow actors. Keya Ghosh, a BJP leader, responded by criticizing Chatterjee's compromise and highlighting the unwavering support of many BJP supporters in the state.

articles.title: The turbulent 15 months of Trump’s unlikely US intelligence director | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Tulsi Gabbard, the former Democrat and former Hawaii representative, resigned as director of national intelligence on Friday.  Her tenure was marked by tension with President Donald Trump, who often excluded her from key conversations and publicly questioned her intelligence assessments. Despite efforts to streamline the agency, Gabbard's relationship with the president deteriorated over time, culminating in a public disagreement about Iran and a perceived partisan approach to her role. Following Gabbard's resignation, Aaron Lukas will serve as acting director until June 30th.

articles.title: Elected government has no role in Jammu demolitions, says Farooq Abdullah - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Farooq Abdullah, president of the National Conference (NC), stated that the elected government has no involvement in the ongoing demolitions in Jammu.  He accused the opposition parties of pursuing anti-Gujjar policies and claimed that Gujjars and Bakerwals have historically protected the region's borders. Gulam Ali Khatana, a BJP Rajya Sabha member, countered by accusing the NC and Congress of neglecting the development of Gujjar and Pahari communities for decades. He praised the Modi government's efforts to empower these communities.

articles.title: SpaceX launches its biggest rocket yet in test flight from Texas | SpaceX | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX launched its largest Starship rocket, a redesigned version dubbed V3, on a test flight from Starbase in Texas. The launch carried 20 mock Starlink satellites and marked the company's 12th attempt to fly the vehicle. NASA, which is funding the project, hopes to use the Starship to land astronauts on the moon as part of its Artemis program.  SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has announced plans for an initial public offering of the company.

articles.title: Rajasthan Cabinet approves new industrial development policy with focus on talent economy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Rajasthan Cabinet approved a new industrial development policy focused on talent economy and private sector participation to create a world-class industrial infrastructure.  Industries and Commerce Minister Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore stated the policy would provide incentives for micro, small, and medium enterprises, one district one product, and the export sector. The policy aims to boost the state's economy to $350 billion by 2028-29.  The Cabinet also approved decisions on energy production, water conservation, and pensioners' welfare.

articles.title: Tulsi Gabbard resigns as Trump’s top US intelligence official | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Tulsi Gabbard, former Democratic congresswoman and presidential candidate, resigned as Donald Trump's director of national intelligence citing her husband's recent diagnosis with a rare form of bone cancer.  She cited her decision to leave the administration in part due to her opposition to US military interventionism, which she has held since serving in the Hawaii National Guard during the Iraq War. The president confirmed Gabbard's resignation and appointed Aaron Lukas as acting director.

articles.title: Uk Airlines Offers: UK airlines EasyJet and Jet2 assure holidaymakers: No extra charges for summer flights despite rising fuel costs | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: easyJet and Jet2 have assured customers that their summer travel plans remain unaffected despite rising jet fuel prices linked to Middle Eastern tensions.  Both airlines stated they had no fuel shortages and would not introduce extra charges for flights or package holidays. However, Kenton Jarvis, chief executive of easyJet, warned that higher oil prices could eventually affect fares later in the summer. Willie Walsh, director general of the International Air Transport Association, cautioned that airlines may have to pass on rising fuel costs to passengers.

articles.title: Protester with ‘Trump is a war criminal’ banner removed from Trump rally in New York state – US politics live | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump held a rally in Rockland county, New York, where he was interrupted twice by protesters. The president then spoke about how his supporters had previously defended him from protestors and claimed that the recent disruptions were "dangerous." Trump also addressed the case of Kilmar Ábrego García, who was deported to El Salvador despite a US court order barring it. He blamed the previous administration for sending Ábrego to the prison, claiming an "administrative error".  The president then spoke about his son's upcoming wedding and claimed that he had been forced to return to Washington due to government matters. Trump boasted about passing a dementia test and recounted a story about a friend who complained about the cost of GLP-1 shots. He also announced Aaron Lukas as acting director of national intelligence after Tulsi Gabbard resigned.

articles.title: Debt and distress: youth caught in cricket betting trap - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Cricket, once a beloved sport in India, has seen a surge in gambling and betting activities.  The rise of online platforms, including mobile apps and websites, has made it easier for individuals to engage in this activity, targeting vulnerable groups such as unemployed youth, students, and daily wage earners. Police are concerned about the expansion of this illegal industry into an international network.

articles.title: Israel’s October 7 tribunal: Show trial of Palestinians or justice? | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel approved a special military tribunal to try Palestinians accused of participating in the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attack.  The tribunal will have the power to impose the death penalty and has drawn criticism from international organizations including the United Nations, which called for its repeal. Human rights groups like Amnesty International and B'tselem condemn the legislation as a way of seeking revenge on imprisoned Palestinians, while some Israeli parliamentarians believe it will bring justice. The tribunal is expected to hold televised trials of an estimated 300 detainees, many of whom are civilians, with concerns raised about potential unfair trials due to coercive practices in security-related cases.  The move has been met with mixed reactions, with some Israelis supporting the tribunal while others call for a state commission of inquiry into the government's role in preventing the attack.

articles.title: Drugged, raped and filmed: German woman alleges years of horrific abuse by ex-partner - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A German woman, 59-year-old Claudia Wuttke, has accused her former partner of drugging and raping her over a period of 16 years, with the alleged crimes captured on video.  Police discovered the videos in June 2025 after finding them on a laptop. The German authorities dropped investigations into 65 of the 67 alleged cases due to statute of limitations laws, leaving only two remaining cases for prosecution. Wuttke expressed her disappointment at the lack of justice and called it "unacceptable" that most of the abuse would go unpunished.

articles.title: Police drop case against artist who depicted high-profile Australians in uniforms with Nazi symbols | New South Wales | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Michael Agzarian, an artist, was charged with displaying Nazi symbols by a public act without lawful excuse after depicting prominent Australians in military uniforms emblazoned with Nazi symbols.  The charges were dropped before the Downing Centre local court on Friday, almost a year after they were filed. Judge Karen Stafford found that the police had reasonable cause to lay the charges but criticized them for taking seven months to withdraw them. Agzarian's lawyer argued that the artwork was political satire and that his client did not know the symbols were Nazi symbols.

articles.title: Vadodara to host Vibrant Gujarat Regional Conference in June - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Vibrant Gujarat Regional Conference (VGRC) will be held in Vadodara in the last week of June 2026, focusing on Central Gujarat's industrial strength and investment opportunities. The conference aims to highlight the region's contributions to manufacturing, including its dominance in sectors like transport equipment, auto components, pharmaceuticals, and beverages.  The event will attract stakeholders from industry, government, and academia, with a focus on tourism and culture. Gujarat is expected to showcase its strengths in these areas, including heritage sites like Sabarmati Ashram and the Statue of Unity.

articles.title: Burnham says politics ‘needs new script’ and vows to change Labour if elected as Makerfield MP – as it happened | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Andy Burnham launched his campaign as the Labour candidate in the Makerfield byelection. He stated that a vote for him is a vote to change Labour and highlighted successes of Greater Manchester and Liverpool since he left Westminster in 2017. The Green party's candidate, Chris Kennedy, withdrew from the ballot just nine hours after being announced.  John Healey, the defence secretary, urged Nigel Farage to provide transparency about a £5 million gift he received from a billionaire businessman.  The UK borrowed more than expected in April due to high inflation, and the Office for National Statistics reported public sector net borrowing of £24.3 billion.

articles.title: US says DRC team must isolate due to Ebola before arriving for World Cup | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Democratic Republic of Congo national football team must isolate for 21 days before entering the US for the World Cup due to an ongoing Ebola outbreak in their country.  Andrew Giuliani, executive director of the White House Task Force for the World Cup, confirmed this requirement, stating that the team must maintain a bubble until June 11th to avoid being denied entry. The team is currently training in Belgium and will play its first World Cup game against Portugal on June 17th in Houston.

articles.title: Waiting for Green Card? Leave US first, re-enter with an immigrant visa - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has announced new guidance directing immigration officers to require individuals on temporary visas, like B1/B2, F1/M1, J1, H-1B, and O-1, to return to their home countries while they wait for their Green Cards. This policy aims to distinguish between temporary admission and permanent residence, with the USCIS director, Joseph Edlow, stating that individuals seeking lawful permanent residency should apply for immigrant visas through the US Department of State before reentering the United States.

articles.title: Judith Chalmers, presenter of TV series Wish You Were Here, dies aged 90 | Television | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Judith Chalmers, the beloved British TV presenter who hosted Wish You Were Here…? for almost three decades, passed away at 90 after a battle with Alzheimer's disease. Her family said she died peacefully at home surrounded by loved ones.  She began her career in broadcasting at age 13 and went on to host numerous popular programs including Come Dancing and Woman’s Hour. Chalmers was known for her warm, approachable style and iconic sun tan, which became synonymous with the travel show. She is survived by her husband of 58 years, Neil Durden-Smith, and son Mark Durden-Smith, a TV presenter himself.

articles.title: US says temporary visa holders should leave to apply for Green Cards | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) issued new guidance stating that obtaining a Green Card within the US is discretionary, not automatic. The Department of Homeland Security said this policy aims to ensure immigration procedures are followed rather than allowing individuals to remain in the US while seeking permanent residency through "loopholes."  Rights groups criticized the move, warning it could force vulnerable migrants to return to unsafe conditions while awaiting decisions on their applications.

articles.title: ‘It would be a big mistake’: WHO Africa chief warns against underestimating Ebola virus risk in Congo, Uganda - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization's Africa director, Mohamed Yakub Janabi, warned against underestimating the risk of the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and neighboring Uganda.  He stated that a single case could trigger wider transmission, emphasizing the need for increased attention to the outbreak due to the lack of a vaccine for the Bundibugyo strain. Janabi urged international cooperation to control the outbreak, highlighting the difficulty in assessing its duration due to the "hyperdynamic movement of people."  Efforts are underway to increase testing, strengthen infection prevention measures, and improve community engagement.

articles.title: Public hearing for limestone mining called off in Meghalaya after protest - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Jaiñtia National Council, Hima Sutnga Youth Federation, Jaiñtia Students' Union
articles.rephrased_article: The authorities in Meghalaya’s East Jaiñtia Hills district canceled a public hearing for a ₹1,800-crore integrated cement plant and limestone mining project after two groups clashed. Supporters of the project and those opposed to it engaged in violence, including the burning of a truck, leaving several people injured. The conflict followed similar clashes on Thursday near the District Magistrate’s office, where police used batons to disperse the groups.  The Jaiñtia National Council, Hima Sutnga Youth Federation, and Jaiñtia Students’ Union** stormed the public hearing site, leading to its cancellation.

articles.title: Wes Streeting insists he can win Labour leadership race despite ‘underdog’ status | Wes Streeting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Wes Streeting, former health secretary, launched a shadow campaign for the Labour leadership, arguing that Keir Starmer is unfit to lead.  He believes he can win over Labour members despite trailing in polls and being seen as right-leaning. Streeting outlined plans including moving families out of temporary accommodation, speeding up the establishment of a national care service, and introducing a wealth tax. He also suggested bringing back environmental impact assessments for large developments and addressing concerns about immigration.  Andy Burnham, who is campaigning to win a byelection in Makerfield, is seen as Streeting's main rival.

articles.title: Slovenia’s parliament approves right-wing Janez Jansa as prime minister | Government News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Slovenia’s parliament voted to approve Janez Jansa, a right-wing populist, as prime minister.  Jansa's appointment follows a post-election stalemate and marks a shift from the country's previous liberal government. The new coalition government, formed by Jansa’s Slovenian Democratic Party (SDS) and several center-right groups, will hold 43 seats in the assembly. Jansa has previously served as prime minister from 2004 to 2008, 2012 to 2013, and 2020 to 2022.  He plans to prioritize economic growth, fighting corruption, and decentralization.

articles.title: Timelapse footage shows giant 'cave' inflated over Paris bridge
articles.rephrased_article: JR, a French artist known for his large-scale art installations, transformed Paris' oldest bridge, the Pont Neuf, overnight into a giant inflatable cave structure called "La Caverne" or "The Cave". The 17th-century landmark was nearly unrecognizable to Parisians until Thursday.  The installation, measuring 120 meters in length and ranging from 12-18 meters in height, will be open to the public starting June 6th and run until June 28th.

articles.title: Pakistan gets its own ‘Cockroach Awaam Party’ as India’s viral CJP sparks cross-border satire wave - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan has seen the emergence of satirical political groups inspired by the Cockroach Janta Party, a viral movement in India.  These groups, such as the Cockroach Awami Party and Cockroach Awami League, have emerged on social media platforms like Instagram and X, mirroring the Indian party's focus on issues affecting unemployed youth, including education, healthcare, and employment opportunities. The Pakistani groups use similar slogans and branding to their Indian counterparts, positioning themselves as alternative voices to mainstream political parties in Pakistan.

articles.title: Public hearing for limestone mining called off in Meghalaya after protest - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: **The authorities in Meghalaya’s East Jaiñtia Hills district canceled a public hearing for a ₹1,800-crore integrated cement plant and limestone mining project after two groups clashed. Supporters of the project and opponents faced off at Lum Syrman, resulting in a truck being set ablaze and minor injuries to some people. The incident followed a similar clash near the District Magistrate’s office on Thursday, prompting police intervention.

articles.title: World Cup: England’s shock squad and the politics of football – The Latest | Soccer | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Thomas Tuchel has selected a significantly different squad for England's World Cup team, omitting key players like Harry Maguire, Trent Alexander-Arnold, Cole Palmer, and Phil Foden. This decision comes as the club season concludes with Arsenal securing its first Premier League title in 22 years.

articles.title: Mahmoud Khalil to appeal US deportation case to Supreme Court | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Mahmoud Khalil, a pro-Palestine advocate, will appeal his deportation case to the Supreme Court after a federal appeals court declined to rehear his case.  Khalil's lawyers argue that he was targeted for his free speech and that the Trump administration exploited immigration enforcement to punish him. The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) supports Khalil's claim, stating that the government can't target individuals based on their protected speech.

articles.title: Power Division warns consumers against fake subsidy links, QR code scams - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Ministry of Energy’s Power Division issued a warning to consumers about fraudulent activities targeting electricity bill subsidies. The Power Division advised against clicking on suspicious links or QR codes, as criminals are attempting to steal personal information through these methods.  Consumers were urged not to share any personal details for obtaining subsidies and law enforcement agencies have been informed of the scam.

articles.title: Why thousands of stock trades tied to Trump are raising eyebrows
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump's name appears on government filings revealing thousands of stock trades made in the first three months of this year. The Trump Organization stated that neither the president, his family, nor the company were involved in selecting or approving investments and receive no advance notice of trading activity.

articles.title: Chudthebuilder Bond Offer: ChudTheBuilder may be released after reported $1M bond offer from crypto casino “Duel” - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: ChudTheBuilder, whose real name is Dalton Eatherly, may soon be released from jail after a crypto gambling platform called Duel offered to pay his $1 million bond. The news has generated significant online discussion, with many questioning the motivations behind the unusual financial offer in connection with the high-profile case involving serious charges related to a courthouse shooting in Tennessee.  The court has not yet confirmed final approval of the bond payment.

articles.title: Punjab government to remove stray dogs from high footfall public spaces following Supreme Court order - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bhagwant Mann, Punjab Chief Minister, announced that the state government will remove stray dogs from all high footfall public spaces as per Supreme Court directions issued on May 19, 2026.  The move aims to ensure public safety and provide relief to citizens concerned about stray dog attacks. The government plans to create adequate shelters for stray dogs while adhering to the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act and ABC Rules regarding euthanasia in cases involving dangerous or rabid animals.

articles.title: ‘Kind of humiliating’: trans community responds to EHRC’s new code of practice | Gender | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Stephen Whittle, a 70-year-old man who advocates for gender recognition, was at the Chelsea flower show when the updated code of practice from the Equality and Human Rights Commission was published. The guidance confirmed that single-sex spaces must be used based on biological sex, leading to mixed reactions. Some welcomed it as a consolidation of last year's court victory, while others expressed concern about its practical implications for trans inclusivity.  Businesses and service providers are grappling with the changes, seeking clarity and time to adapt their policies.

articles.title: Premier League finale: Arsenal, relegation, Champions League, Salah and Pep | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Premier League season concludes with all 10 matches kicking off simultaneously, featuring a relegation battle and European qualification fights. Arsenal will lift the title after Manchester City failed to win their match against Bournemouth.  Tottenham Hotspur and West Ham United are vying for survival in the final day's drama. Liverpool, Bournemouth, and Aston Villa are battling for Champions League spots, with Mohamed Salah's future at Liverpool uncertain after his public criticisms of the team's style.  Pep Guardiola is leaving Manchester City after a decade of success, with Enzo Maresca rumored to be his successor.

articles.title: ‘Most relentlessly cruel’: Gaza flotilla activists tell harrowing accounts of abuse in Israeli custody - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Mousa Taher, a New Zealand activist, and other activists from the Global Sumud humanitarian aid flotilla, recounted harrowing experiences of abuse they endured while detained by Israeli forces.  Taher described being subjected to torture, including being bound tightly with plastic zip ties, having his face stepped on, and being beaten. He also said that Israeli soldiers recognized him and addressed him by name because he had previously been detained. Isselmou Ould Maloum, a Mauritanian activist, echoed similar accounts of violence, stating that the Israeli military lacks a strategy other than using force against Palestinians.  Gregory Terry, an American activist, described the detention as "miserable" and said his fellow activists suffered broken bones and were repeatedly tased. Juliet Lamont, an Australian activist, recounted being subjected to sexual assault and physical violence during their time on board the flotilla. All of these activists expressed their determination to continue protesting for Palestinian freedom.

articles.title: Twisha Sharma: Rival claims of murder and suicide set off media frenzy after Indian bride dies
articles.rephrased_article: A dowry death case in India has sparked a media frenzy after the death of 33-year-old model and actor Twisha Sharma.  Twisha's parents allege she was tortured by her husband, Samarth Singh, and his mother, retired judge Giribala Singh, over dowry demands and that she was murdered. The police have lodged a case against the Singhs and are investigating whether her death was murder or suicide. Giribala Singh denies the allegations, claiming Twisha had mental health issues and committed suicide.  The case has drawn attention to the issue of dowry deaths in India, where thousands of women are murdered annually for bringing insufficient dowries.

articles.title: UK pitched single market for goods with EU in pursuit of deeper trade ties | Brexit | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The UK government proposed a single market for goods with the EU as a means to reintegrate British trade. However, EU officials rejected this idea and suggested alternatives like a customs union or economic alignment through the European Economic Area.  Despite these setbacks, both sides are seeking agreements on food and agricultural products, emissions trading schemes, and youth mobility programs. The UK government is also pursuing closer defense cooperation with the EU. While negotiations remain stalled on defining a future agenda, both sides hope to announce deals before a summit tentatively scheduled for July 13th.

articles.title: Lucky Motors partners with China's GAC as it bets fuel shock will drive EV switch - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Lucky Motors, a Pakistani conglomerate, is launching EVs in partnership with Guangzhou Automobile Group (GAC) and plans local assembly by December 2026.  The move comes amid rising fuel prices and increased interest in solar energy, which the company believes will accelerate EV adoption. The CEO of Lucky Motors, Muhammad Faisal, expects initial imported stock to sell out quickly.  Lucky Motors, which also assembles smartphones, is exploring local battery manufacturing and plans to export Pakistani-assembled vehicles to other right-hand drive markets.

articles.title: What are the implications of US sanctions in Lebanon? | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States has imposed sanctions on nine individuals, including two Lebanese military officers, accused of ties to Hezbollah. The sanctions come as Israel continues its attacks on Lebanon despite a ceasefire and amid efforts by Washington to facilitate further talks between Lebanese and Israeli officials.

articles.title: French Open 2026: Aryna Sabalenka cuts short news conference as top players protest over Grand Slam prize money - BBC Sport
articles.rephrased_article: Aryna Sabalenka, Iga Swiatek, and other top players protested the French Open's prize money by limiting their media commitments to 15 minutes.  The players, who are demanding a higher percentage of revenue be allocated to prize money, player welfare, and more consultation in decision-making, believe the current system is inadequate. Novak Djokovic did not participate but supported the principle behind the action. The French Open tournament director expressed confidence that the issue will be resolved while players remain open to further discussions.

articles.title: 'West wants to impose homosexuality on the rest of the world': Senegal PM makes shocking claim - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Senegal's Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko defended the country's new anti-LGBTQ law, arguing that it reflects the will of the Senegalese people and is not influenced by Western pressure.  Sonko criticized Western countries, accusing them of imposing their values on other nations. He stated that while Senegal faces criticism from some international organizations like the UN, they do not have to follow these practices. The new law significantly increases penalties for same-sex relations in the country, prompting concern from human rights groups and activists.

articles.title: Mumbai, Maharashtra emerging as key hubs for global investment and clean energy partnerships, say diplomats - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Consul Generals from Australia and Finland highlighted the growing investment opportunities in Mumbai and Maharashtra, emphasizing infrastructure development, clean energy, education, and technology sectors.  They praised Mumbai's transformation, citing projects like the Coastal Road and metro expansion as drivers of investor confidence. Both diplomats acknowledged challenges faced by foreign investors, including regulatory clarity and streamlined approval systems. Despite these challenges, they expressed optimism about Mumbai's long-term trajectory as a global economic hub.

articles.title: Meta and Snapchat blocking Saudi dissidents’ accounts | Social media | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Meta, Instagram, and X have blocked accounts of Saudi Arabian dissidents, following orders from the Saudi government. The move has been met with criticism from human rights groups who argue that these companies are effectively silencing dissent and aiding in repression.  At least seven accounts were blocked by Meta at the end of April, including those of two American citizens and two individuals based in Europe. Snapchat appears to have slowed or removed some accounts without notifying users, while X, owned by Elon Musk, has informed some users that their content was blocked due to a request from the Saudi government.

articles.title: US releases second batch of government declassified UFO files - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The United States’ Defense Department released a second batch of classified files on alleged UFO sightings, including reports of green orbs, discs, and fireballs.  These documents, ordered by President Donald Trump, follow a disclosure process that began in the late 1970s. The release includes documentation from a top-secret facility in Sandia, New Mexico, where there were 209 reported sightings between 1948 and 1950. Experts have said the first batch of released files did not provide conclusive evidence of alien technology or extraterrestrial life.

articles.title: San Diego’s Muslims, a mosque, and a city shaken | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The San Diego Muslim community is grieving after an attack that shattered their sense of safety.  The attack has prompted the community to come together and support each other as they try to move forward.

articles.title: Carney says Alberta is 'essential' to Canada as province plans vote on separation
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Mark Carney stated that Alberta is an "essential" part of Canada, while Alberta Premier Danielle Smith announced a referendum on October 19th to determine whether the province should remain in Canada or pursue independence. The vote comes after pressure from a growing separatist movement and a recent legal challenge by First Nations groups halted the process of verifying petition signatures.  Smith maintains that Albertans deserve a say in their future, despite criticism from various organizations, including the Sturgeon Lake Cree Nation and the New Democratic Party.

articles.title: 'Go home' for Green Card rule: Immigration attorney Rahul Reddy explains what H-1B visa holders should do now - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The USCIS has issued a new memo that requires individuals seeking Green Cards to apply for visas in their home countries instead of adjusting status within the United States. The memo, which experts say may be challenged in court, emphasizes that approving Green Card applications from within the US is a "favor" and not a right.  The memo's impact on those who have already filed Green Card applications remains unclear, but it suggests individuals with pending I-140 petitions should consult legal counsel to strengthen their case.

articles.title: Infrastructure is foundation of economic growth, says M. Jamshed - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M. Jamshed, during a special address at The Hindu’s Maharashtra Infrastructure Conclave 2026, highlighted the crucial role of infrastructure in development, emphasizing its importance for India's economic growth. He praised Maharashtra as a leading example of infrastructure development from Delhi's perspective and expressed optimism about the state's continued success.  Mr. Jamshed noted that the Centre's focus on integrated infrastructure development since 2014 has expanded beyond traditional sectors, encompassing physical, digital, and social infrastructure. He emphasized core sectors like roads, railways, maritime transport, and energy alongside digital and social infrastructure segments such as rural drinking water, sanitation, and water resource management.

articles.title: Flotilla video: Ben-Gvir’s template of televised abuse was honed on Palestinians | Israel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Itamar Ben-Gvir, Israel's national security minister, has been widely criticized for publicly celebrating abuse of detainees in Israeli jails.  He shared a video of the mistreatment of activists intercepted at sea attempting to deliver aid to Gaza, prompting condemnation from numerous countries and even the US ambassador to Israel. While Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli Prime Minister, condemned Ben-Gvir's actions, he has previously failed to address systemic abuse against Palestinians in custody.  This incident highlights a pattern of escalating violence and human rights violations against Palestinians under his leadership, with calls for sanctions and international intervention growing louder.

articles.title: NCCIA uncovers gang selling data of govt officials to foreign entities; four arrested - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) arrested four individuals in South Punjab for selling sensitive personal data of government officers to foreign entities. The suspects, identified as Arshad Tariq, Arham Bari, Anam Sabir and Mohammad Rizwan, were allegedly sharing the data with foreign intelligence agencies.  The NCCIA is investigating how the information was accessed and has directed government institutions to strengthen data security.

articles.title: Bolivia in crisis: Social unrest, demands for president to resign escalate | Protests News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Rodrigo Paz, Bolivia's president, is facing growing social unrest and demands for his resignation.  The protests began over a convergence of sector-based demands, including wage increases, contaminated fuel issues, and land classification changes. Indigenous groups from the highlands escalated the protests by blocking roads, demanding the president step down. Former President Evo Morales, who was ousted in 2019, has mobilized his supporters to pressure President Paz. The government is attempting to address legitimate demands while also cracking down on those deemed hostile to democracy.  The unrest has led to violence and clashes between protesters and police, with over 120 people detained.  Jose Luis Lupo, the Presidency Minister, stated that the government will use dialogue for legitimate sectors and full force of the law against those attacking democracy. The situation remains fluid as authorities seek a path forward.

articles.title: Judge drops criminal case against Kilmar Abrego Garcia
articles.rephrased_article: A US federal judge dismissed the criminal case against Kilmar Abrego Garcia, who was wrongfully deported to El Salvador last year. The judge ruled that the charges were politically motivated, stating the government only pursued them after Abrego Garcia successfully challenged his removal and the Executive Branch reopened its investigation into a 2022 traffic stop incident.  The justice department has not yet commented on the decision.

articles.title: US stocks today: Dow hits record high as Middle East hopes lift sentiment and Warsh takes Fed charge - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The S&P 500 closed at a new high, marking its eighth consecutive weekly gain.  Semiconductor stocks were mostly higher, driven by gains in Qualcomm and Lenovo Group's strong quarterly results. The Federal Reserve welcomed new Chair Kevin Warsh, while Estee Lauder rose after ending merger talks with Puig.   The U.S. made progress toward a deal with Iran, though more work remains according to Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

articles.title: Danny Go: YouTube star Danny Go mourns heartbreaking loss of 14-year-old son Isaac - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Danny Go, a popular YouTuber known for his family-friendly show "Danny Go!", announced the death of his 14-year-old son, Isaac, who had been battling stage 3 mouth cancer since late 2025.  Go shared a heartfelt tribute on Instagram, expressing his immense love and pride in his son's strength despite facing health challenges. Fans and fellow creators have expressed condolences and support for the family during this difficult time. Go canceled his tour to focus on supporting Isaac and creating special memories with him.

articles.title: Woman sustains injury at Kochi metro worksite - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A young woman was injured in a freak accident when an iron piece from the worksite of Kochi Metro Rail Limited (KMRL) fell on her car near Padivattom. The incident occurred during de-shuttering work and caused damage to her windshield.  Afcons Infrastructure, the contractor, has been asked to suspend work until further notice and provide support and compensation to the injured woman. An inquiry will be conducted to determine the cause of the accident and strengthen safety measures.

articles.title: Qatar sends mediators to Tehran in sign talks to reopen strait of Hormuz are reaching climax | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Qatar has dispatched a team of mediators to Tehran in an effort to facilitate talks regarding the Strait of Hormuz. The aim is to sign a memorandum of understanding that would lead to 30 days of discussions on Iran’s nuclear program, deferring discussion of the US demand for the Iranian stockpile of highly enriched uranium. Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, stated that while some progress has been made, the US will not accept Iran imposing tolls on commercial shipping through the strait.  Pakistan is currently considered the main interlocutor for the US in these negotiations.

articles.title: PTI workers stage protests in various cities, defy Section 144 in Islamabad - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: PTI and TTAP organized protests across Pakistan on Friday, demanding the release of former prime minister Imran Khan and addressing concerns over inflation, rising petroleum prices, and deteriorating law and order.  PTI Islamabad President Aamir Mughal, along with other leaders, held a protest in Islamabad despite Section 144 being in place, while Shandana Gulzar from TTAP spoke at a press conference in Peshawar, highlighting the plight of civilians in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and accusing the federal government of mismanagement. These protests were joined by political and social activists across the country, including those from the Haqooq-i-Khalq Party.

articles.title: US judge dismisses indictment against Kilmar Abrego Garcia | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A US District Judge dismissed an indictment against Kilmar Abrego Garcia, finding that he would not have been prosecuted if he hadn't challenged his deportation. The judge stated the Department of Justice only reopened its human smuggling probe stemming from a 2022 traffic stop after Abrego Garcia filed his lawsuit.  The case was dismissed due to the timing of the charges, which were seen as retaliatory by the court.

articles.title: Gaza flotilla activists allege abuse by Israeli forces while detained
articles.rephrased_article: Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand confirmed that her officials have received information detailing the "appalling abuse" of Canadian citizens detained in Israel following the interception of a Gaza-bound aid flotilla. Germany and Spain also reported injuries among their nationals, while organizers of the Global Sumud Flotilla alleged at least 15 cases of sexual assaults and other mistreatment.  The Israeli prison service dismissed the allegations as false, stating all detainees were held in accordance with the law.

articles.title: ‘I always hear them before I see them’: Drones strike fear in Colombia | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The use of drones by armed groups in Colombia has significantly increased, posing a serious threat to civilians. The Colombian Ministry of Defence reported 8,395 weaponized drone attacks in 2025, with the number rising sharply from 61 incidents in 2024. These drones are used for both attack and surveillance purposes, enabling armed groups to target infrastructure, police, and the army.  The proliferation of drones has been driven by their affordability and ease of use, allowing groups like the ELN, Clan del Golfo, and FARC dissidents to engage in combat with less risk to themselves. The Colombian government is attempting to counter this threat with anti-drone systems, but armed groups are finding ways around these technologies.  The constant presence of drones has created a climate of fear for civilians, forcing them to live under the constant threat of attack and destruction.

articles.title: Tulsi Gabbard resigns as US director of national intelligence
articles.rephrased_article: Tulsi Gabbard, the US director of national intelligence under President Donald Trump, will resign from her position on June 30th.  She cited her husband's recent bone cancer diagnosis as the reason for her departure, stating she cannot continue in her role while he faces this challenge. Trump expressed his support for Gabbard and noted her "incredible job" during her tenure.  Aaron Lukas, the principal deputy director, will assume the acting director position.

articles.title: Marco Rubio: Trump ‘disappointment’ with Nato will be discussed at summit | Nato | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump expressed disappointment with Nato allies for not becoming more actively involved in attacking Iran, setting the stage for a potentially contentious summit. Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, emphasized that the rift would be addressed at the July meeting in Ankara and discussed potential military assistance from Nato countries to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if peace talks with Iran fail.  The US is also planning to adjust troop numbers in Europe, although the exact cut remains unclear. Some allies expressed confusion about the White House's erratic policy changes, while others provided limited support for the US attack on Iran.

articles.title: Colgate-Palmolive India Q4 profit down marginally to Rs 353 cr; FY26 revenue dips to Rs 6,124 cr - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Colgate-Palmolive India Ltd (CPIL) reported a 9% year-on-year increase in net profit after tax, excluding one-offs and exceptional items, to Rs 355 crore for the March quarter of FY26. Sales also rose by 9%, reaching Rs 1,582.77 crore. CPIL's Managing Director & CEO Prabha Narasimhan highlighted the company's focus on premiumization and driving consumption, which contributed to the growth. The company's total income increased by 8.8% to Rs 1,612.22 crore for the quarter.  The company declared a second interim dividend of Rs 24 per share.

articles.title: UAE spooked? Fearing Gulf chaos, Abu Dhabi joins Saudis, Qatar in urging Trump against fresh Iran war - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar have urged US President Donald Trump to avoid restarting military action against Iran and instead pursue diplomacy. These Gulf states are concerned that renewed hostilities could trigger retaliation from Tehran and destabilize the region's economy.  They argue that military action would not achieve Washington’s long-standing objectives with Iran, and they differ on the type of diplomatic arrangement the US should pursue. Despite recent progress in talks between Iran and the US, concerns remain about a permanent deal being reached and the potential for renewed conflict if negotiations fail.

articles.title: Ahead of kharif season, Dharwad Deputy Commissioner warns traders of strict action ‘creating artificial scarcity’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Deputy Commissioner Snehal R. of Dharwad district held a video conference with officials, seed and fertilizer dealers, and farmer leaders to address concerns about the upcoming monsoon season and ensure timely availability of seeds and fertilizer. Ms. Snehal warned against unfair trade practices and directed officials to monitor market conditions, set up vigilance squads, and report on seed and fertilizer availability.  She assured farmers that sufficient quantities of seeds and fertilizer were available in Dharwad for the kharif season and urged them to purchase from authorized sources like Raitha Samparka Kendras and fertilizer sale centres.

articles.title: Actor Momina Iqbal seeks FIR against PML-N MPA over alleged blackmail and harassment - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Momina Iqbal, an actor and model, filed a first information report (FIR) against PML-N MPA Saqib Chadhar for blackmail, harassment, and death threats.  Iqbal alleged that Chadhar began threatening her after she refused his marriage proposal, claiming he was already married to two women. She also provided evidence of the threats through WhatsApp messages and video calls. Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz warned against any political pressure or attempts to exploit the situation for personal gain, stating the matter will be addressed strictly according to law.

articles.title: From Palestine to Catalonia, Guardiola believed in more than just football | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pep Guardiola, the legendary Manchester City manager, is stepping down after a decade of success.  He has used his platform to advocate for various causes beyond football, including Palestinian children in Gaza and homelessness in the UK. His outspokenness on these issues, while widely praised, also drew criticism from some groups, particularly regarding his comments about the Jewish community. Guardiola's legacy extends far beyond trophies won, as he has consistently used his influence to speak up for social justice.

articles.title: Why is the US putting pressure on Cuba and what are Trump's aims?
articles.rephrased_article: The United States is escalating pressure on Cuba, accusing the country of posing a national security threat and recently indicting former leader Raúl Castro. The US has imposed an oil blockade, sanctions, and a murder indictment against Castro, citing an incident in 1996 where Cuban fighter jets shot down two civilian planes owned by Cuban exiles.  Cuba maintains its actions were justified as self-defense within its airspace and accuses the US of using the charges to justify military aggression. The US has also targeted senior Cuban officials accused of human rights abuses or corruption, while offering $100 million in aid through humanitarian organizations. Cuba's response has been characterized by fiery rhetoric, with leaders demanding an end to the blockade and accusing the US of "coercion" and threats. China and Russia have condemned the US pressure on Cuba.

articles.title: Czech president urges Nato to ‘show its teeth’ over Russia’s provocations | Nato | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Petr Pavel, the Czech president, urged NATO to take a more assertive stance against Russia's provocations.  He suggested various measures like cutting off Russian banks from global financial systems and shooting down violating aircraft. Pavel emphasized the need for decisive responses to deter further aggression by Moscow, citing Russia's disregard for diplomatic solutions and its willingness to escalate tensions. He also called for increased pressure on Russia from the United States, particularly through tougher sanctions tied to a potential peace settlement in Ukraine.  Despite domestic disagreements with the Czech government, Pavel remains committed to pushing NATO forward on this issue.

articles.title: Kevin Warsh takes over US Fed with a policy problem already in view - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Federal Reserve's new chair, Jerome Powell, faces a challenging task as he navigates the complex economic landscape.  Christopher Waller, a Fed Governor who has recently shifted his stance on monetary policy, is advocating for a possible rate hike to combat rising inflation. The debate over policy is intensifying, with Powell facing pressure from colleagues and market sentiment that favors tighter monetary policy. Powell will need to weigh the impact of his decisions on both inflation and maximum employment, while also navigating potential conflicts with the Trump administration's economic agenda.  The Fed's next meeting on June 16-17 will be crucial as they vote on interest rates and new economic projections.

articles.title: Quote of the day by English physicist Brian Cox: “We explore because we are curious, not because we wish to develop grand views of reality or better widgets.” | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Brian Cox's quote, "We explore because we are curious, not because we wish to develop grand views of reality or better widgets," highlights the inherent value of curiosity in human exploration.  While modern societies often prioritize practical outcomes and measurable results, history demonstrates that many significant discoveries began without immediate applications. Cox emphasizes that exploration is driven by a desire to understand what is unknown, regardless of potential future benefits. This quote challenges the assumption that all exploration must have an immediate purpose or tangible result.

articles.title: Rubio's maiden India visit aims to repair strained ties; boost Quad cooperation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio will visit India from May 23 to 26, 2026, aiming to repair strained bilateral ties.  He will meet with External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and attend a Quad Foreign Ministers meeting in New Delhi. The trip follows a recent three-day visit by India's Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri to Washington DC focused on stabilizing the relationship.  The talks are expected to focus on bolstering ties in energy, trade, investment, critical technology, and people-to-people exchanges, as well as discussing the West Asia crisis and its economic impact.

articles.title: Tulsi Gabbard resigns as Trump's top US intelligence official - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Tulsi Gabbard resigned as President Donald Trump's director of national intelligence, citing her husband's diagnosis with a rare form of bone cancer. She informed Trump during an Oval Office meeting on Friday and the resignation is effective June 30th.  Aaron Lukas, the Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence, will serve as acting director while Gabbard focuses on supporting her husband.

articles.title: Canada’s Carney says Alberta is ‘essential’ as province mulls separation | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney emphasized the importance of Alberta to Canada's economy, stating that he is working with the province to improve it.  Premier Danielle Smith announced a referendum on whether Alberta should remain part of Canada or hold a vote for separation. The decision came after a court blocked a petition to hold a vote on separation, citing lack of consultation with Indigenous groups. Smith stated she opposes separation but believes in respecting the democratic rights of Albertans and that she will respect the results of the referendum.  Conservative Party Leader Pierre Poilievre said he would campaign against separation, while some Liberals criticized Smith for stoking separatist sentiment for political gains.

articles.title: Bodies of Italian divers did not have optimal equipment, says rescuer
articles.rephrased_article: A Finnish diver who participated in the recovery of the bodies of four Italian scuba divers in a Maldivian cave said the equipment found with them was not optimal and that they were not using underwater caving gear. The divers, including Prof Monica Montefalcone and research fellow Muriel Oddenino from the University of Genoa, entered the water on May 14th at Vaavu Atoll but failed to resurface later.  The bodies were recovered by a team of Finnish and Maldivian divers, with one Maldivian rescue diver dying while searching for them. An investigation is ongoing into the cause of the accident.

articles.title: State-sponsored apprenticeships and decriminalising cannabis on the bill at Victoria’s Labor conference | Jacinta Allan | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jacinta Allan, Victorian Premier, will announce a plan to create a government-owned electricity body that will hire electrical apprentices at the Labor party's final state conference before the election. The plan aims to address workforce shortages in the industry and is inspired by her father's experience as a linesman at the State Electricity Commission (SEC).  The conference will also feature discussions on various policy proposals, including reducing workweeks, increasing reproductive health leave, decriminalizing cannabis, and addressing issues like public transport affordability.

articles.title: BSE 100 rejig: Paytm, Ashok Leyland and CG Power enter index; Adani Group-owned Ambuja, 2 more exit - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The BSE Index Services announced changes to the BSE Sensex and BSE Sensex Next 50 indices, effective today.  Ambuja Cements, Tube Investments, Paytm, Ashok Leyland, and CG Power were among companies that saw significant shifts in their positions within these indexes. The additions of TVS Motor Company, Ashok Leyland, One 97 Communications, and CG Power and Industrial Solutions to the BSE Sensex Next 50 are notable changes ahead of its implementation on June 22, 2026.

articles.title: Shocking reality of 100 families living beneath Manila highways in the Philippines | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Families living beneath elevated expressways in Manila, Philippines, have adapted to a life of limited space and constant noise.  They've created makeshift homes from salvaged materials and rely on informal work for income. Despite the challenges posed by traffic noise, flooding, and sanitation issues, residents maintain routines, build social ties, and find moments of happiness within their cramped living conditions. The settlements remain largely hidden from public view, offering a glimpse into the resilience and resourcefulness of those who call these areas home.

articles.title: KERC directs Escoms to give consumers 15 clear days to pay bills - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka Electricity Regulatory Commission (KERC) has mandated that all electricity distribution companies provide consumers with a minimum of 15 days to pay their bills from the actual bill issuance date, not the scheduled billing date. The order, effective June 1st, requires all bills to clearly state the generation date and time, and mandates payment due dates be calculated accordingly.  The commission emphasized that late or extended billing cycles do not exempt Escoms from providing consumers with sufficient payment time.

articles.title: Govt reduces petrol by Rs6 per litre, high-speed diesel by Rs6.8 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The government reduced the price of petrol by Rs6 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs6.80 on Friday, bringing the new prices to Rs403.78 per litre for petrol and Rs402.78 per litre for HSD. This is the second consecutive week of fuel price reductions, following a series of adjustments made in response to global market fluctuations and the ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran. The government has been adjusting petroleum prices weekly since the conflict began, aiming to mitigate its impact on consumers while balancing budgetary considerations.

articles.title: Pakistan’s army chief in Iran as US’s Rubio says ‘slight progress’ in talks | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan’s army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, is in Tehran to mediate between Israel and the United States, as part of ongoing efforts to end their war.  Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Esmaeil Baghaei, stated that while progress has been made, a deal is not yet close. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio reported "slight progress" in talks with Iran, but emphasized the need for continued negotiations. The European Union announced it will impose new sanctions on Iranian officials and others responsible for blocking the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Russia's Putin vows retaliation after accusing Ukraine of hitting student dormitory
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin of Russia vowed retaliation after accusing Ukraine of a deadly attack on a student dormitory in the occupied Luhansk region.  Six people were killed and 39 injured, with 15 missing, according to Putin. Ukraine's military claimed the strike targeted the headquarters of Russia's elite Rubicon drone unit, alleging it was responsible for striking civilians and civilian infrastructure.  Zelensky, the Ukrainian president, previously reported the FSB headquarters in Kherson was hit, resulting in casualties.

articles.title: US judge dismisses criminal indictment against Kilmar Ábrego García | Kilmar Ábrego García | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A US judge dismissed a criminal indictment against Kilmar Ábrego García, finding that the Trump administration would not have prosecuted him had he not challenged his deportation.  Ábrego García, who entered the United States without authorization, became a symbol of the Trump administration's mass deportations after being sent to El Salvador's notorious anti-terrorism prison, Cecot. The White House initially opposed his return but was ordered by the Supreme Court to facilitate it. Ábrego García pleaded not guilty, arguing he was being prosecuted in retaliation for suing the government.

articles.title: Gaza flotilla activists allege sexual assault and rape in Israeli detention | Israel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Activists released from Israeli custody following their detention on a flotilla attempting to deliver aid to Gaza have alleged abuse, including sexual assaults and injuries.  Israel’s prison service denies the allegations, stating all detainees are treated in accordance with the law and medical care is provided according to professional judgment. Several countries, including Germany, Italy, and France, reported injuries and accusations of serious misconduct, prompting investigations into possible crimes like kidnapping and sexual assault.  The incident has further strained relations between Israel and international organizations and governments.

articles.title: NTPC Green Energy Q4 Results: Cons PAT declines 15% YoY to Rs 197 crore despite 47% revenue uptick - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Despite a 47% revenue growth to Rs 913 crore in Q4FY26, the state-run company saw its profit fall to Rs 247 crore from Rs 307 crore in the same period last year. The decline was attributed to a sharp rise in expenses, which increased by 60% to Rs 713 crore, driven by factors like employee benefits and finance costs.  However, PAT surged multi-fold sequentially, reaching Rs 247 crore from Rs 17 crore in Q3FY26.

articles.title: Massive, absurd: Immigration experts, foreign-born founder react to new Green Card rule - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: USCIS has issued a memo requiring all visa holders in the US to leave and apply for Green Cards from their home countries. The agency argues that visa holders come to the US temporarily, while Green Cards are for permanent residents, creating a conflict of intent. Nick Davidov, founder of a Russian-origin venture capital firm, criticized the policy, stating it would force top scientists and entrepreneurs to leave the country and wait years for their applications to be processed. Immigration specialist James Blunt echoed these concerns, highlighting that even former First Lady Melania Trump could have been subject to this rule. Legal experts believe the memo is vague and will likely be challenged in court as it deviates from Congress's intent when establishing the H-1B visa program.

articles.title: Bowring Hospital wall collapse: Lokayukta probe finds major safety lapses - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Lokayukta inquiry into the fatal wall collapse at the Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital in Shivajinagar, Karnataka, has revealed multiple structural and administrative failures. The investigation found that the wall was constructed beyond permissible height limits, had been damaged previously, and lacked proper drainage systems and retaining walls.  The inquiry also highlighted negligence by authorities who failed to monitor dangerous structures and encroachments. Senior IAS and IPS officers, officials from various departments, and hospital authorities appeared before the Lokayukta for questioning. The Lokayukta directed authorities to identify similar unsafe structures and take preventive measures.

articles.title: Kevin Warsh sworn in as new US Fed chair | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.sentiment_target: United States Federal Reserve Board of Governors
articles.rephrased_article: Kevin Warsh was sworn in as the new chair of the United States Federal Reserve Board of Governors, succeeding Jerome Powell.  Warsh's appointment comes amid political pressure on the historically non-partisan institution and a contentious nomination process.  He will lead the central bank at a time when inflation is rising, with consumer prices increasing 0.6 percent in April and energy prices surging.  The first policy meeting Warsh will lead is scheduled for June 16-17.

articles.title: Ebola risk now at highest level in DR Congo, says WHO - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organisation (WHO) has raised the risk assessment level for the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo to very high, citing a rapidly spreading epidemic with nearly 750 suspected cases and 177 suspected deaths.  Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO chief, emphasized the urgency of containing the virus, particularly due to violence and insecurity hindering response efforts. While Uganda's situation is stable, WHO has deployed international staff and prioritized existing treatments like monoclonal antibodies and olibdesivir for clinical trials.

articles.title: Nascar legend Kyle Busch dies aged 41
articles.rephrased_article: Kyle Busch, a two-time Nascar Cup Series champion, died at age 41. The Busch family, Richard Childress Racing, and Nascar announced the sudden passing of the racing legend who was ninth on the circuit's all-time win list.  Tributes poured in from fellow drivers and organizations, including former teammate Denny Hamlin, Brad Keselowski, Speedway Motorsports, and Dale Earnhardt Jr., who remembered Busch as a "champion among champions" and a "once-in-a-generation competitor."

articles.title: Soft power sell-off: anger as British Council announces sale of historic Madrid building | Foreign policy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The British Council, a global organization promoting understanding between the UK and other countries, is facing backlash from staff over proposed cuts and restructuring. Staff in Spain are protesting the sale of its Madrid headquarters, with concerns about job security and leadership decisions. The organization is struggling to pay off a £197 million debt incurred during the Covid-era, prompting drastic measures including potential sales of buildings in other European countries.  The British Council maintains it remains committed to its mission but acknowledges the financial challenges and is taking steps to ensure its long-term sustainability.

articles.title: Sebi bars seven entities in social media stock recommendations, alleges Rs 58 crore gains - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sebi, India's market regulator, has accused seven individuals and a group of entities, including Rohan Gupta and Sharon Gupta, of manipulating stock prices through social media influence. The regulator conducted searches between January 21-24, 2026, after observing unusual trading patterns linked to the group's online activity. Sebi alleges that the group accumulated shares before recommending them on social media platforms, profiting from price increases following retail investor participation in those stocks.  The regulator found a significant increase in trade value and profits for the group during the examination period.

articles.title: US spy chief Tulsi Gabbard resigns under pressure from White House: Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Tulsi Gabbard, the US Director of National Intelligence, resigned from her position to support her husband, who has been diagnosed with an extremely rare form of bone cancer.  She informed President Donald Trump of her decision during a meeting in the Oval Office on Friday and plans to leave her post on June 30th. Gabbard acknowledged progress made at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, but stated that there is still important work to be done before her departure.

articles.title: ACB books Medchal deputy collector in disproportionate assets case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) officials conducted searches on Marri Vamshi Mohan, a Special Grade Deputy Collector, and his associates following allegations of acquiring assets beyond known sources of income. The searches uncovered properties valued at around ₹6.22 crore, including land plots, houses, and vehicles, along with cash and gold ornaments. Vamshi Mohan was arrested and remanded to judicial custody.  The investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: WHO says 12th person infected with hantavirus detected in the Netherlands | Health News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) confirmed a 12th hantavirus case in the Netherlands, involving a Dutch crew member on the MV Hondius cruise ship.  Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO chief, urged countries to continue monitoring passengers and cautioned against further spread. The infected crew member is isolated at a hospital while over 600 contacts are being monitored in 30 countries. The Dutch National Institute for Public Health and the Environment (RIVM) stated that the chance of further spread remains low.

articles.title: Renowned infectious diseases expert Dr Naseem Salahuddin passes away - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Naseem Salahuddin, a renowned infectious diseases expert and professor emeritus at Indus Hospital, passed away on Friday.  The hospital expressed its sorrow over her passing, noting her dedication to patient care, medical education, and humanitarian service. Dr. Salahuddin was a member of the World Health Organization’s Expert Advisory Panel on Rabies since 2004 and played a pivotal role in raising awareness about rabies prevention and treatment. She also authored books and contributed to various scholarly journals and news outlets including Dawn.

articles.title: Tennessee execution called off after failed lethal injection
articles.rephrased_article: A Tennessee execution of Tony Carruthers, convicted of kidnapping and murdering three people in 1994, was postponed after staff were unable to find a suitable vein for the lethal injection.  The Department of Corrections stated that while they found a primary IV line, they could not establish a backup line as required by protocol. Governor Bill Lee granted Carruthers a temporary reprieve from execution for one year. The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) and other advocates have raised concerns about the trial's integrity and called for DNA testing. Kim Kardashian also joined the cause, urging supporters to demand the evidence be tested before it's too late.

articles.title: Canadian prime minister says Alberta ‘essential’ to country as separatists push for independence | Canada | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mark Carney, the Canadian prime minister, emphasized that Alberta is crucial to Canada's future.  Following a judge's ruling halting an independence referendum petition, Danielle Smith, Alberta's premier, vowed to hold a vote on whether to initiate the legal process for a binding referendum in October. Smith maintains she supports Alberta remaining within Canada but believes a public debate is necessary.  Carney expressed support for Canada and its future while acknowledging that Alberta plays a vital role.

articles.title: Deepa Jewellers, Cotec Healthcare receive Sebi approval for IPOs - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Deepa Jewellers, a Hyderabad-based company specializing in hallmarked gold jewelry processing and trading, plans to raise funds through an IPO consisting of a fresh issue and offer-for-sale. The IPO will include up to Rs 250 crore worth of shares from the company and up to 1.18 crore shares offered for sale by promoters Ashish Agarwal and Seema Agarwal.  Cotec Healthcare, a contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) serving pharmaceutical companies, also received Sebi approval for its IPO. The company manufactures formulations across various therapeutic segments and operates a manufacturing facility in Roorkee with an installed capacity of over 4 billion units.

articles.title: 'I can not in good conscience...': What Tulsi Gabbard wrote about her husband in her resignation letter - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Tulsi Gabbard, the Director of National Intelligence, submitted her resignation, effective June 30, 2026.  She cited her husband's recent diagnosis with a rare form of bone cancer as the reason for her departure. Gabbard stated that she needed to step away from her duties to support her husband and ensure he could face his illness alone. Joe Kent, Gabbard's deputy, resigned in March.

articles.title: Conference on higher education held - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jebi Mather, MP, emphasized the need for continuous modernization of Kerala's higher education sector during a conference on 'Higher Education Reforms'.  Prof. Junaid Bushiri, Vice-Chancellor of Cochin University of Science and Technology, highlighted the importance of developing employability skills alongside academic achievements. The conference, organized by Kerala Principals’ Council, featured sessions led by prominent figures in academia and literature.

articles.title: Gaza flotilla activists allege abuse, sexual assault in Israeli detention | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Global Sumud Flotilla organizers allege at least 15 cases of sexual assault and other abuse against freed activists who were abducted from international waters by Israeli forces. The allegations, which include claims of being stripped, kicked, tasered, and denied access to a lawyer, have been reported by activists who returned to their home countries and are under investigation by authorities in Italy, Germany, and Spain.  The Israeli prison service denies the allegations, stating that all detainees are held according to the law with full regard for their basic rights.

articles.title: CDF Asim Munir arrives in Iran as part of ongoing mediation efforts: ISPR - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Field Marshal Asim Munir, the Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff (COAS), arrived in Tehran on Friday evening to mediate between the US and Iran.  He met with Iranian officials including Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. The visit comes amid ongoing Pakistani efforts to facilitate peace talks after a previous round of negotiations fell through. Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, praised Pakistan's role in mediating the conflict and acknowledged that the primary interlocutor on this issue has been Pakistan.  The visit underscores the urgency for de-escalation between the two countries as tensions remain high over issues like Iran’s nuclear program, sanctions relief, and regional security concerns.
