articles.title: Waymo pauses robotaxis in four Texas cities and Atlanta over flooded road risk
articles.rephrased_article: Waymo has paused its robotaxi service in five US cities, including Atlanta and San Antonio, due to a software issue that has led some vehicles to drive into flooded roads. The company issued a recall of nearly 3,800 robotaxis after an incident on April 20th in San Antonio, Texas. Waymo stated it is working on additional software safeguards and expects to resume service soon.  The company also temporarily suspended its service on freeways in San Francisco, Los Angeles, Phoenix, and Miami while evaluating its cars' performance in construction zones.

articles.title: Suspected Ebola cases triple in a week as WHO warns of rapid spread in DRC | Global development | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) has revised its threat assessment for the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo to "very high," citing a rapid spread and increasing number of suspected cases. The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo strain, is concentrated in Ituri province with some cases reported elsewhere in the country and neighboring Uganda. Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO director-general, highlighted the need to address distrust among local communities for successful response efforts while acknowledging a "good sign" of improved detection rates.  Despite these challenges, Dr Anne Ancia, WHO representative in the DRC, remains optimistic about containing the outbreak.

articles.title: Nobel Prize winner Olga Tokarczuk under fire after revealing she uses AI to develop ideas | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Olga Tokarczuk, the 2018 Nobel Prize winner in Literature, sparked controversy after remarks at Impact’26 in Poznań where she discussed using AI for brainstorming and research. While acknowledging the potential of AI to enhance creativity, she clarified that her upcoming novel was not written with AI and primarily uses it for fact-checking.  Her comments drew criticism from some Polish writers who saw them as an endorsement of AI-written fiction, but she later issued a clarification stating she uses AI as a tool to support traditional writing practices. The debate surrounding Tokarczuk's remarks highlights the ongoing discussion about the role of AI in artistic creation and its impact on authorship.

articles.title: Four from Telangana State colleges to go on Sakura Science Programme - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Four students from Telangana have been selected to participate in the Japan Science and Technology Agency’s (JST) SAKURA Science Programme. The seven-day program, starting May 24th, will allow the students to visit advanced scientific institutions, interact with scientists, and gain exposure to Japan's innovation in education and science. The students were selected through district-level nominations and a state-level screening test conducted earlier this year.

articles.title: ‘Full-on summer heat’: western Europe braces for unusually high temperatures | Europe | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Météo-France and the Met Office have issued warnings for extreme heat across western Europe, with temperatures expected to exceed 30C in several countries.  The heat is attributed to a high-pressure system trapping hot air from Morocco under the influence of an anticyclone. The French national weather forecaster predicts record-breaking temperatures for May in France and Brittany, while the Met Office issued "extraordinary" heat health alerts for the UK, with potential highs exceeding 33C.  The heat wave is expected to last several days and could bring record high temperatures across Spain as well.

articles.title: India battles power cuts as heatwave boosts electricity demand to record - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: India is experiencing power cuts due to record-breaking heat and high electricity demand exceeding 270 gigawatts. The government has urged consumers to conserve energy, with outages lasting from 40 minutes to an hour in some areas like Chennai.  Grid-India, the national regulator, reported a peak deficit of 2.57 gigawatts late Thursday evening. Experts suggest that India needs to accelerate battery storage development to manage surplus solar energy during nighttime hours.

articles.title: Australian man dies after falling down ravine on hike to Machu Picchu
articles.rephrased_article: A 52-year-old Australian man, Matthew Cameron Paton, died after falling down a ravine while hiking the Inca Trail to Machu Picchu in Peru. Paton was reported missing on Wednesday after he fell through a broken railing while with a group of tourists and a guide.  His body was found by members of the High Mountain Rescue Unit in Cusco. Authorities are investigating the cause of the fall, and Paton's family described him as a devoted husband and father who had always wanted to travel to Peru.

articles.title: Turkiye shutters liberal Istanbul university seized in criminal probe | Education News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Recep Tayyip Erdogan revoked the operating license for Istanbul Bilgi University, a private university known for its liberal values, citing insufficient education standards. The closure, effective immediately, follows a criminal investigation into the institution's parent company and has sparked protests from students who will now continue their studies at Mimar Sinan University. The Council of Higher Education promised to ensure student safety during this transition.

articles.title: Did China spy on Elon Musk, other tech executives during Trump's Beijing visit? Blogger makes big claim - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Independent blogger and author Jennifer Zeng claims China spied on US President Donald Trump's two-day visit to Beijing last week, alleging that disguised military personnel monitored the delegation. Zeng accused a server standing behind billionaire Elon Musk of being a "highly decorated active-duty Chinese military officer" and another waitress of being an "elite battalion commander."  Zeng has previously accused China of involvement in the killing of Khalistani terrorist Hardeep Singh Nijjar in Canada.

articles.title: LTM to acquire Randstad’s tech, consulting businesses for €160 million - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: LTM, formerly LTIMindtree, has proposed to acquire Randstad's Technology and Consulting Services business in several European countries for €160 million. The acquisition, expected to be completed by Q3 of fiscal 2027, aims to expand LTM’s presence in key markets and provide local expertise in digital engineering, cybersecurity, and IoT.  The deal also includes a five-year IT services partnership with Randstad's India Global Capability Center and a strategic talent MSP for LTM's expanding global workforce.

articles.title: Carlo Petrini, Slow Food movement founder, dies aged 76 | Italy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Carlo Petrini, the founder of the Slow Food movement, has died at age 76.  He led the organization, which promotes sustainable and local cuisine since its inception in 1986, until 2022. President Sergio Mattarella and Italian agriculture minister Francesco Lollobrigida both expressed their condolences, highlighting Petrini's impact on food culture and sustainability. The movement has grown to be active in over 160 countries, including a significant presence in Britain where it was supported by King Charles.  Petrini's legacy will continue through the global Slow Food movement he helped create.

articles.title: Pakistan, Turkiye air forces reaffirm ‘growing strategic convergence’ in defence sector: ISPR - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan Air Force Chief of Staff ACM Zaheer Ahmed Baber Sidhu visited Turkey, meeting with Turkish Air Force Commander General Ziya Cemal Kadıoğlu, Defence Minister Yaşar Güler, and Baykar Technologies Chief Technology Officer Selçuk Bayraktar.  During the meetings, both sides reaffirmed their commitment to enhancing collaboration in defence, aerospace innovation, and emerging technologies. The air chief also discussed joint exercises, training programs, and professional exchanges with Turkish officials.

articles.title: Elon Musk's SpaceX postpones Starship launch as mega share sale looms
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX has postponed its Starship launch due to a malfunctioning hydraulic pin on the launch tower, with an attempt scheduled for Friday. The delay comes ahead of SpaceX's record-breaking IPO on the Nasdaq stock market, which could make Elon Musk, already the world's richest person, the first trillionaire.  The uncrewed launch will mark the debut of Starship V3, a powerful rocket designed to carry 100 metric tons and support future missions.

articles.title: Marco Rubio visits India: What’s at stake with Trump-Modi ties strained? | International Trade News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, is visiting India for a three-day trip ahead of the Quad meeting on May 26th.  Rubio's visit comes amidst strained relations between Donald Trump and Narendra Modi, as well as efforts to mend ties with India. The visit also coincides with the US Department of Justice dropping criminal fraud charges against Indian billionaire Gautam Adani, and an extension of a sanctions waiver allowing purchases of Russian oil.  Rubio's trip is seen as part of Washington's effort to strengthen bilateral relations with India, particularly in light of tensions between Trump and Modi last year.

articles.title: Indian man sentenced to 15.5 years in prison for gold scam in US, picked 16 gold bars from elderly victims - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Syed M Makki, a 38-year-old Indian man, was sentenced to 15.5 years in prison for his role in a gold scam targeting elderly victims across the US.  The scheme involved malware that tricked victims into believing they were dealing with legitimate authorities, leading them to liquidate their savings and purchase gold bullion. Makki acted as a courier, collecting gold bars from victims and delivering them to co-conspirators. The Justice Department reported that the scam resulted in over $4.75 million in losses for victims.

articles.title: Over 2.3 lakh students register for TNEA 2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Over 2.34 lakh candidates have registered for the Tamil Nadu Engineering Admissions (TNEA) 2026 portal, with many completing application and fee payment processes. The registration deadline is June 2nd, followed by certificate uploads until June 6th.  Random number assignments will occur on June 5th, with certificate verification starting June 8th and a rank list published on June 29th. Counselling for special category students, including those in the eminent sportspersons category, is expected to begin in July after Class XII results are released.

articles.title: Estée Lauder ends merger talks with Gaultier owner Puig | Retail industry | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Estée Lauder and its Spanish rival Puig have ended merger talks that would have created a $40 billion beauty group. The talks stalled over disagreements about the compensation demanded by Charlotte Tilbury, a key brand owned by Puig.  The termination of the discussions was welcomed by Estée Lauder investors, whose shares rose after the news.

articles.title: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto inaugurates 39km-long Shahrah-i-Bhutto linking Qayyumabad to M9 Motorway - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari inaugurated the 39-kilometer Shahrah-i-Bhutto Expressway, linking Karachi's Qayyumabad to the M-9 Motorway.  He also laid the foundation stone for a new expressway project connecting Karachi Port to Qayyumabad. Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah highlighted the expressway's six interchanges, lanes, and elevated section, emphasizing its potential to reduce travel time by an hour. Bilawal Bhutto Zardari emphasized the PPP's commitment to public-private partnerships in developing Karachi and Pakistan, citing projects worth billions of rupees underway. He also announced plans for a Sindh International Financial Centre and a defense production zone in Karachi.

articles.title: UK scientists developing Ebola vaccine that could be ready for trials in months
articles.rephrased_article: Oxford University scientists are developing a new Ebola vaccine using the same technology employed during the COVID-19 pandemic. The experimental vaccine, which uses a modified chimpanzee cold virus to deliver genetic material about the Bundibugyo species of Ebola virus, could be ready for clinical trials in two to three months. The World Health Organization (WHO) has upgraded the risk level from "high" to "very high" in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where the outbreak is centered. The vaccine will likely be used through ring vaccination, targeting those most at risk of infection and close contacts of infected individuals.

articles.title: Why is Trump deploying 5,000 troops to Poland? | NATO News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump announced the deployment of 5,000 additional troops to Poland, a move that contradicts recent Pentagon decisions to reduce US forces in Europe. The announcement was made following a public row between Trump and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz over the US-Israeli war on Iran and has been linked to Trump's increasingly transactional approach to alliances.  Poland's right-wing president, Karol Nawrocki, welcomed the move, while other NATO allies like Germany and Spain have also expressed support for the deployment. The Pentagon has not yet confirmed whether these troops are the same as those previously planned for Germany or if they will be redeployed from elsewhere in Europe.

articles.title: Arvind Panagariya’s advice to RBI: ‘100 is just a number; let rupee depreciate or reserves will bleed out’ - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The 16th Finance Commission Chairman, Panagariya, urged the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) not to be swayed by the psychological impact of the Rs 100-per-dollar mark when formulating policy decisions. He argued that a depreciation in the rupee is the appropriate response to current oil price fluctuations, regardless of their duration.  He cautioned against relying on temporary measures like dollar-denominated sovereign bonds or high-interest NRI deposits to support the currency and warned that artificially defending the rupee would deplete foreign exchange reserves.

articles.title: UK military air show Royal International Air Tattoo cancelled amid Middle East conflict concerns | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Royal International Air Tattoo (RIAT), a major military air show held annually at RAF Fairford, has been cancelled this year due to uncertainty surrounding the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The United States Air Force and organizers cited concerns about access to the base as the reason for the cancellation. The event, which regularly attracts over 170,000 visitors, will not take place from July 17-19.  Organizers are offering ticket holders refunds, transfers to the 2027 event, or donations to the RAF Charitable Trust.

articles.title: Tribal areas on forest fringes in Chamarajanagar promised electricity and drinking water soon - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
articles.rephrased_article: The Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has approved proposals for electricity and drinking water to tribal areas on the forest fringes in Chamarajanagar district.  Bhupender Yadav, Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, communicated this decision to Sunil Bose, Lok Sabha MP for the district. The approvals are expected to bring electricity to tribal families living in darkness and provide tap water connections to Palar habitation.

articles.title: Australian government plans for ‘worst-case scenario’ retail fuel rationing, documents reveal | Energy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Australian government has outlined plans for retail fuel rationing as the International Energy Agency warns of an impending oil market crisis. The federal energy minister, Chris Bowen, can declare a liquid fuel emergency (LFE) and implement rationing measures under the Liquid Fuels Emergency Act if industry-led solutions prove inadequate.  While the government initially ruled out the need for rationing, documents reveal discussions about potential rationing scenarios, including limiting purchase amounts per vehicle.

articles.title: CDF Asim Munir leaves for official visit to Iran: security sources - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, the Chief of Defence Forces, is currently in Iran on an official visit where he will discuss US-Iran talks, peace in the region, and other important issues. Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, praised Pakistan's role in mediating a peace deal between Washington and Tehran, stating that Pakistan has been the primary interlocutor throughout the process.  Meanwhile, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met with Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi to review proposals for resolving disputes during his visit to Tehran. Despite ongoing diplomatic efforts, differences over Iran's nuclear program, sanctions relief, and regional security concerns remain a major obstacle to progress in negotiations.

articles.title: Ebola risk raised to 'very high' in DR Congo
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) has raised the Ebola risk in the Democratic Republic of Congo to "very high" due to the outbreak's rapid spread and fatality rate.  Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO head, stated that while the risk is high in the region and globally, it remains low at a global level. The outbreak has resulted in 177 suspected deaths and 750 suspected cases so far, with no proven vaccine for the rare Bundibugyo strain.  Scientists are developing new vaccines, but their effectiveness remains uncertain.

articles.title: Oil prices rise as investors doubt breakthrough in US-Iran peace talks - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Oil prices rose on Friday but were still headed for a weekly loss as investors remained cautious about the prospects of a US-Iran peace deal. Brent crude futures increased by $1.66, or 1.6%, to $104.24 a barrel while US West Texas Intermediate futures rose by $1.11, or 1.2%, at $97.46.  Analysts predict that oil prices will remain elevated due to supply disruptions caused by the war in Ukraine and concerns about global economic growth.

articles.title: Slow Food founder Carlo Petrini dies aged 76 in Italy
articles.rephrased_article: Carlo Petrini, founder of the Slow Food movement, passed away at age 76 in his Italian hometown.  He established the organization in response to protests against the opening of the first McDonald's in Italy and led it for decades, promoting sustainable food production and traditional cooking practices. His work connected communities worldwide and earned him friendships with figures like King Charles III and Pope Francis. The movement emphasizes quality, environmental sustainability, and fair conditions for producers.

articles.title: Standard Chartered boss apologises for ‘lower-value human capital’ comments amid job cuts | Standard Chartered | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Standard Chartered chief executive Bill Winters apologized for using the term "lower-value human capital" to describe employees facing job losses due to artificial intelligence.  Winters, in a series of posts on LinkedIn, attempted to clarify his comments about automation and employee transition but faced criticism for his choice of words. The bank plans to cut 15% of its back-office roles by 2030, impacting employees in several locations.

articles.title: Markets to enter prolonged “drag phase,” not deep correction: Vikas Khemani - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Khemani, managing director of a prominent investment firm, stated that while corporate earnings have held up well, the full impact of global disruptions like the war in Ukraine is yet to be seen. He believes markets are prepared for these impacts and do not expect significant earnings growth in Q1.  He remains optimistic about India's domestic growth story, citing strong consumer demand and a resilient investment cycle. Khemani advises investors to focus on bottom-up stock selection rather than broad market trends, highlighting opportunities in manufacturing, pharma, CDMO, BFSI, and IT. He cautions against chasing FOMO and emphasizes the importance of long-term diversification strategies based on individual goals.

articles.title: Humanity’s home in space is shutting down: What comes next will be nothing like it | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: NASA has decided to transition away from owning and operating the International Space Station (ISS) and instead fund multiple private companies to build commercial space stations.  These stations will provide research opportunities, manufacturing capabilities, and space tourism services. Vast Space, Axiom Space, Orbital Reef, and Starlab are among the companies developing these platforms. The transition aims to reduce costs and drive innovation in human spaceflight. While the timeline for commercial alternatives is optimistic, experts acknowledge potential risks associated with a gap between the ISS's retirement and their availability.

articles.title: Will TVK government take ‘firm stand’ on Mekedatu project, asks Palaniswami - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Edappadi K. Palaniswami, general secretary of the AIADMK, questioned the Tamil Nadu government's ability to protect its interests in the Mekedatu balancing reservoir project on the Cauvery river, citing the reported support of the Congress party and concerns about potential power-sharing agreements.  D.K. Shivakumar, Karnataka’s Deputy Chief Minister, reportedly stated that Tamil Nadu had no right to object to the project, while T.T.V. Dhinakaran, founder of the AMMK, echoed these concerns.

articles.title: Man City confirm Guardiola exit to end decade-long, trophy-laden spell | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pep Guardiola is stepping down as Manchester City manager after a decade in charge, bringing an end to one of the most successful eras in English football.  He leaves with 20 trophies won, including six Premier League titles and the Champions League. Guardiola's departure follows a disappointing season where City finished second in the league, despite winning the domestic cup double this season. He will be succeeded by his former assistant, Mikel Arteta.

articles.title: Pep Guardiola to end decade-long Manchester City reign at end of season - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pep Guardiola will step down as Manchester City manager at the end of the season after a decade in charge.  He has won six Premier League titles, three FA Cups, five League Cups, and the Champions League during his tenure but has not secured a league title in two years. Guardiola cited personal reasons for leaving, stating that "nothing is eternal." Enzo Maresca, who previously worked with Guardiola at City, is reportedly set to take over as manager.

articles.title: Kim Soo-hyun: AI used to fake evidence that ended South Korean actor's career, say police
articles.rephrased_article: South Korean police are seeking an arrest warrant for a YouTuber, Kim Se-ui, who allegedly faked evidence to defame actor Kim Soo-hyun. The YouTuber manipulated screenshots of text messages and shared an audio file made with AI to falsely portray the actor as having dated actress Kim Sae-ron when she was underage.  The allegations led to Kim Soo-hyun's career downfall, prompting him to seek legal action against the YouTuber and the actress' family.

articles.title: Trump’s ‘disappointment’ with Nato lays groundwork for ‘one of the most important’ summits ever, Rubio says – Europe live | World news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The upcoming NATO summit in Ankara will address Trump's disappointment with the alliance's response to US operations in the Middle East.  Rutte, Malmer Stenergard, and other officials emphasized the need for increased defense spending, industrial capacity building, and a stronger commitment to Article 5.  Meanwhile, protests erupted against the new US consulate opening in Greenland after comments by the special envoy suggesting a return of US influence on the territory. The summit also saw discussions about Iran's nuclear program and efforts to restore freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Bank Nifty near key resistance zone; breakout above 54,300 crucial: Ajit Mishra - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nifty has been consolidating for the second week, with upside capped near 24,000.  Bank Nifty has shown stronger performance, gaining around 1 percent and approaching the 54,300–54,350 resistance zone. Ajit Mishra, a market analyst, suggests traders focus on defined-risk strategies like bull call spreads in both indices due to the expiry week. He also highlights opportunities across sectors, including IT, pharma, healthcare, energy, and auto, with specific stocks like Angel One and Trent showing potential for further gains.

articles.title: How a failed attempt to protect a tablecloth led to Jacques E. Brandenberger’s invention of “cellophane” | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jacques E. Brandenberger, a Swiss inventor born in 1872, accidentally discovered Cellophane while trying to create stain-resistant fabric.  Inspired by observing wine being spilled on a tablecloth, he developed a flexible cellulose film that became widely used in food packaging and consumer goods due to its transparency and protective qualities. The invention revolutionized retail packing, offering consumers the ability to view products before purchase, and paved the way for modern transparent packaging. Cellophane, while initially intended for textiles, has become a symbol of modernity and hygiene, with its biodegradability making it an attractive alternative to single-use plastics in today's market.

articles.title: Minority commission recommends upgrading Pallikkal govt. school in Wayanad - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Kerala State Commission for Minorities recommended that the Pallikkal Government Lower Primary (LP) School in Wayanad be upgraded to an upper primary (UP) school during the 2026-27 academic year. The recommendation was made following a petition submitted by the school's management and favorable response from the Wayanad Deputy Director of Education, who acknowledged the school's facilities and student population.  The school has all necessary infrastructure for an UP section, including smart classrooms and additional construction under the Wayanad Package.

articles.title: Iran’s enriched uranium stockpile: Can it be safely transferred? | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump reiterated that the US will not allow Iran to keep its enriched uranium stockpile, while Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei issued a directive prohibiting the removal of the uranium from Iranian soil.  The future of the estimated 440kg of highly enriched uranium remains a sticking point in peace negotiations between the US and Iran. While experts say it is possible to transfer enriched uranium safely, concerns remain about its potential for misuse. The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has specific protocols for transporting enriched uranium hexafluoride, but the issue of transferring this material safely from Iran remains unresolved.

articles.title: Prince Rahim Aga Khan arrives in Gilgit-Baltistan - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prince Rahim al-Hussaini Aga Khan V arrived in Pakistan on Wednesday for a week-long visit, marking his first since being named the spiritual leader of the Ismaili community last year. He was welcomed by officials at the airport in Gilgit and will be accorded state guest status during his stay.  He has met with President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, and PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari since arriving. Prince Rahim is expected to attend public gatherings and address ceremonies throughout the country.

articles.title: Turkish opposition fights court ousting of leaders in ruling boosting Erdogan
articles.rephrased_article: The Turkish opposition, led by Özgür Özel of the Republican People's Party (CHP), is challenging a court ruling removing them from leadership positions. The appeals court declared the 2023 leadership election null and void, prompting protests and criticism from opposition leaders who accuse President Recep Tayyip Erdogan of seeking to eliminate rivals.  The ruling has sparked concerns about the future of Turkey's political landscape and potential for snap elections.

articles.title: UN’s climate crisis vote shows political momentum is growing, say experts | Climate crisis | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The United Nations General Assembly overwhelmingly voted in favor of a landmark climate crisis ruling, urging states to transition away from fossil fuels and phase out inefficient subsidies.  While the advisory opinion by the International Court of Justice was hailed as a "historic win" for small island states, its impact on diplomacy has been limited. The resolution, co-sponsored by 90 countries, aims to encourage nations to integrate the ICJ's findings into their climate plans and support domestic legislation.  Despite opposition from major fossil fuel producers like the US, the resolution garnered significant support, demonstrating growing political momentum for climate action.

articles.title: Picked wrong Melody? Parle Industries shares hit 5% upper circuit for 3rd day - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: During a visit to Italy, Prime Minister Narendra Modi gifted Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni a bag of candies called "Melody." The viral video of the exchange sparked interest in Indian brands and led to marketing campaigns by companies like Air India.  The candy's maker, Parle Products, confirmed it is exported to 100 countries. While Parle Industries shares saw a significant jump following the incident, the company has no immediate plans for an initial public offering.

articles.title: 38.5% drop in H-1B registrations for FY 2027: Immigration attorney says numbers were like this 10 years ago - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The USCIS released the details of the H-1B FY 2027 lottery, reporting a 38.5% drop in registrations compared to the previous year.  The agency attributed this decline to President Donald Trump's America First policies and emphasized the shift towards prioritizing highly skilled foreign workers with advanced degrees and higher salaries. The new wage-based selection system saw an increase in applicants with advanced degrees, leading to a 71.5% representation of selected aliens holding a U.S. master’s degree or higher.  Immigration attorney Emily Neumann suggests that the drop is largely due to the $100,000 fee imposed by Trump on applications from outside the United States.

articles.title: RO systems should be maintained properly to be effective, says study - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A recent study in Chennai, India, found that while reverse osmosis (RO) systems effectively remove microbes under ideal conditions, they are not a guarantee for safe drinking water. The study, published in the Journal of Exposure Science & Environmental Epidemiology, revealed that 31% of post-RO samples still contained Escherichia coli (E. coli), compared to 71% in untreated water.  The researchers found a correlation between education level and E. coli contamination, with higher levels of education associated with lower rates of contamination. The study emphasizes the need for proper maintenance and hygiene practices alongside reliable piped water supply and affordable servicing structures to ensure safe drinking water access.

articles.title: Everest record holder warns of Nepal danger as two Indian mountaineers die | Mount Everest News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Two Indian climbers, Sandeep Are and Arun Kumar Tiwari, died on Mount Everest while descending after summiting. Kami Rita Sherpa, a Nepali climber who holds the record for most ascents of Everest, expressed concern about overcrowding on the mountain.  Nepal has issued 492 permits for foreigners this season, with approximately 600 climbers having summited since April. The high number of climbers has raised concerns about safety and potential overcrowding.

articles.title: Anmol alias Pinky sent to jail on judicial remand in narcotics, murder cases - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Anmol, also known as Pinky, an alleged drug queenpin, was sent to jail on a 14-day judicial remand in multiple narcotics cases and a murder case.  She had already been booked in over a dozen criminal cases prior to her arrest earlier this month. Karachi police sought the Sindh government's permission to dispatch a team to Punjab to arrest Anmol’s brothers, ex-husbands, and other co-suspects involved in the drug trafficking network. A Lahore court allowed an FIR against Rana Muhammad Akram, Anmol’s former husband, who allegedly conducted an illegal raid on Yasmeen Tabassam's house.

articles.title: Cubans grapple with fuel shortages and blackouts as US steps up pressure
articles.rephrased_article: Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel has called the US charges against former president Raúl Castro "a political manoeuvre, devoid of any legal foundation." US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has declared Cuba a "national security threat" and the likelihood of a peaceful agreement is low.  The US has imposed a near-total fuel blockade that has affected daily life in Cuba, leading to blackouts and shortages. While some Cubans are struggling with power outages and limited access to essential services, others are finding temporary housing solutions amidst the crisis.  Despite these challenges, many Cubans remain defiant and believe they can withstand any potential US military action.

articles.title: Venezuelan makeup artist who was deported to El Salvador seeks asylum in Spain: ‘I feel safe here’ | US immigration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Andry José Hernández Romero, a Venezuelan man who was deported from the US to El Salvador's notorious Cecot prison under the Trump administration, has moved to Spain seeking asylum.  He fled Venezuela due to persecution as a gay man and alleges he was wrongly accused of gang affiliation by the US government. Lindsay Toczylowski, his lawyer, believes Hernández should be able to clear his name and return to the US, but legal options are limited.  Pedro Sánchez, the Spanish prime minister, has announced plans to grant asylum status to 500,000 migrant workers, including many Venezuelans, offering a potential haven for Hernández. He hopes Spain's liberal immigration policies will afford him better treatment than he received in the US or Venezuela.

articles.title: Turkiye's Erdogan shuts Istanbul Bilgi University seized by state in criminal probe - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Turkey's government revoked the operational license of Istanbul Bilgi University, forcing its closure, citing insufficient educational standards. The decision was made after the university was seized last year as part of a criminal investigation into Can Holding, which owned the institution.  The university, with over 20,000 students from Turkey and abroad, is known for its liberal politics and participation in the Erasmus exchange program.  Students will continue their studies at the Mimar Sinan University of Fine Arts, the university's guarantor school.

articles.title: Tony Abbott to become new Liberal party president in former PM’s return to political frontlines | Tony Abbott | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Tony Abbott, the former Australian prime minister, will become the new president of the Liberal party.  He was unanimously elected after his sole opponent, former foreign minister Alexander Downer, chose to run for vice-president. The election will be confirmed at the Liberal party's federal council meeting next weekend. Abbott will succeed John Olsen and return to active politics after losing his seat in 2019.  Moderate Liberals are concerned about Abbott's potential influence on party direction, particularly regarding immigration. Meanwhile, the Victorian Liberal party state council is holding a meeting where former federal director Brian Loughnane, who is married to Peta Credlin, is expected to be elected as president.

articles.title: US to send 5,000 more troops to Poland, Trump says
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump announced the US will send an additional 5,000 troops to Poland, a move welcomed by Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte.  The decision comes after the Pentagon cancelled a planned deployment of 4,000 troops to Poland last week. Senator Marco Rubio, who is attending a meeting of foreign ministers in Sweden, expressed disappointment with some NATO allies' response to US operations in the Middle East and said that the US continues to have global commitments that require troop re-evaluation.  The move follows Trump's criticism of German Chancellor Friedrich Merz over Iran negotiations and his withdrawal of troops from Germany.

articles.title: MTAR Tech shares soar 24% in just three sessions. What’s triggering this renewed buying spree? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: MTAR Technologies, a Hyderabad-based precision engineering company, secured a new order worth Rs 467.30 crore from an international company, continuing its strong business momentum. This follows the company's recent announcement of a Rs 2,279 crore order from another international client.  The company has revised its FY27 revenue growth guidance upward to more than 80% and expects margins of around 24%. MTAR Technologies also reported strong financial results for FY26 with a net profit increase of nearly 78%, driven by higher product sales and robust order book execution.

articles.title: NCERT book row: SC modifies earlier order concerning 3 academics - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court on Friday reversed its March 11 order that directed the Centre, States, and others to disassociate from three academics involved in a controversial chapter of the NCERT's Class 8 social science textbook. The court left it up to the Centre, states, universities, and institutions to make their own decisions regarding the issue without being influenced by its previous observations.  The Court also clarified that its comments were made in context of the content and not the individuals involved.

articles.title: In 2002, cavers found a hidden skeleton that revealed an ancient Australian predator | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A group of cavers discovered the bones of a marsupial lion, an extinct apex predator, in a limestone cave on the Nullarbor Plain of southern Australia. The discovery was made possible by the cave's stable environment, which has preserved the fossil for millions of years due to its lack of air movement and limited water penetration.  The findings offer a unique glimpse into the extinct ecosystem of the continent and provide valuable insights into the bone density, predatory biting power, and climbing mechanics of the marsupial lion.

articles.title: US raises threat of military action against Cuba | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Secretary of State Marco Rubio and President Donald Trump have issued new threats of military action against Cuba, citing the country's ties to US adversaries Russia and China as national security threats.  Rubio stated that a negotiated agreement is the US preference but that diplomacy with Cuba is not high on their priority list due to the country's broken economic system. Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez condemned the accusations of being a threat, calling them false and intended to instigate military aggression. The US has imposed numerous sanctions on Cuba, implemented a fuel blockade, and increased military presence in the region, raising tensions between the two countries.

articles.title: IHC bans killing of stray dogs, orders authorities to implement humane methods of population control - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has banned the killing of stray dogs in the federal capital, ordering authorities to implement a humane population control program. The court ruled that mass killing of animals is not consistent with Islamic law or international principles and directed the Metropolitan Corporation Islamabad, the Capital Development Authority (CDA), and other relevant bodies to ensure no inhumane actions are taken against stray dogs.  The court also ordered the creation of an advisory committee, a dog bite database, and improved waste management in residential and commercial areas.

articles.title: Slow-moving bands of heavy rain trigger flooding and landslides in parts of China | China | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Heavy rainfall across southern and central China has led to flash flooding, landslides, and waterlogging. The Bay of Bengal, South China Sea, and Pacific Ocean contributed to the prolonged downpour that caused 12 deaths and forced evacuations.  Meanwhile, extreme heat warnings have been issued for northern India, with temperatures exceeding 40°C (104°F) in several regions. These conditions are expected to persist until Wednesday when thunderstorms may develop.

articles.title: Tanzanian police official Faustine Mafwele sanctioned by US for alleged human rights abuses
articles.rephrased_article: The US has sanctioned Faustine Jackson Mafwele, a senior Tanzanian police official, for alleged involvement in the torture and sexual assault of rights activists Boniface Mwangi and Agather Atuhaire.  This action comes amid growing scrutiny of Tanzania's human rights record, with US lawmakers calling for tougher action against the government. The sanctions bar Mafwele from entering the US, while Tanzania's Foreign Affairs Minister Mahmoud Thabit Kombo stated that the government has yet to receive the formal designation.  The US State Department cited "credible information" linking Mafwele to gross human rights violations, and Amnesty International previously called for an investigation into the activists' detention and alleged abuse.

articles.title: ITC has paid dividends worth Rs 90 per share since 2020. Should you buy? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ITC announced a significant dividend payout of Rs 14.50 per share for FY26, marking its largest dividend in nearly six years. The FMCG company's total dividend payout for the fiscal year stands at Rs 14.50 per share with a face value of Re 1 each. Shareholders will receive the dividend between July 24 and 29, contingent upon approval from shareholders at the upcoming Annual General Meeting on July 23rd. The company also reported a 5% year-on-year growth in net profit for Q4 FY26 to Rs 5,113 crore, driven by a strong performance within its cigarettes business and FMCG-cigarettes segment.

articles.title: After CM Vijay’s order to revive Amma Canteens, AIADMK hopes for comeback of other legacy schemes - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: AIADMK functionaries have called for the revival and strengthening of several welfare schemes implemented during the party's previous tenures, including Amma Canteens, Amma Salt, Cradle Baby scheme, Amma Scooters, and 'Gold for Thali'. They also criticized the Tamil Nadu government's handling of government properties and alleged that several welfare programs initiated by the previous AIADMK regime have been discontinued or poorly implemented.  These criticisms were made during a meeting with the newly elected government led by C. Joseph Vijay.

articles.title: In 2000, an amateur explorer found a hidden cave in France filled with ancient art and burials | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Marc Delluc, a cave explorer, discovered Cussac Cave in the Dordogne region of France. The cave contains untouched Upper Palaeolithic art, including detailed animal carvings and human skeletal remains dating back 25,000 to 30,000 years ago.  Analysis suggests the cave was used for both artistic expression and burial rituals, with evidence of intentional burial practices and sophisticated footwear. Cussac Cave is now protected by the French government to preserve its delicate artwork and historical significance.

articles.title: Lebanon’s economy struggles under renewed war and global fuel crisis | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The ongoing war in Lebanon, coupled with global fuel and economic crises, is severely impacting the nation's economy. Hezbollah and Israel's intensified attacks have led to widespread displacement, destroyed infrastructure, and increased prices for essential goods like oil. The World Bank estimates that reconstruction costs could reach $11 billion, while the Finance Minister predicts losses of approximately $3 billion in 2026.  The economic downturn has exacerbated existing societal divisions, with political analysts suggesting that Israel is intentionally exploiting these tensions to maintain control.  Economists warn that Lebanon's economy may become unviable without significant intervention and a return to stability.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz says Pakistan taking measures on a priority basis to increase foreign investment - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met with a delegation from Qatar’s Taameer Group, led by its founder Mohammad Al Ali.  The meeting focused on increasing foreign investment in Pakistan, with Sharif highlighting the removal of obstacles hindering investment and emphasizing Pakistan's potential in sectors like tourism, hospitality, real estate, and construction. The Taameer Group expressed interest in investing in these areas and has already begun work on several projects.

articles.title: US arms sales to Taiwan on ‘pause’ due to Iran war, says acting navy chief | Taiwan | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: US acting navy secretary, Hung Cao, announced a pause in arms sales to Taiwan, citing the need for munitions for its operations against Iran.  Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, and Pete Hegseth, the Pentagon chief, will decide on the future of the $14 billion weapons package. Taiwan’s presidential office spokesperson, Karen Kuo, stated that Taipei has not received any information about adjustments to the arms sale. This announcement comes after a week of heightened tension between Washington and Beijing, with Trump's recent statements suggesting he may be willing to break with US policy on Taiwan.

articles.title: Africa summit in India postponed over Ebola outbreak fears
articles.rephrased_article: The India-Africa Forum Summit, scheduled for May 28-31 in Delhi, has been postponed due to the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda. The World Health Organization declared the latest outbreak a public health emergency of international concern, with over 600 suspected cases and 139 deaths reported so far.  The postponement was announced jointly by India and the African Union, citing the "emerging public health situation in the continent."

articles.title: Nifty Bank rises 650 points as report says RBI unlikely to hike rates to defend rupee; Axis, ICICI, HDFC shares jump up to 2% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is considering various options to address inflation, which remains subdued despite the rupee's recent decline.  While the RBI has stated it will prioritize inflation over currency defense, economists at Standard Chartered predict rate hikes as early as June, citing rising crude prices. Interest rate swap markets are pricing in significant rate increases by the RBI, with some predicting a 50 basis point hike in June and more than 100 basis points over the next year.  The RBI's decision on whether to raise rates will be announced on June 5th, following its second meeting since the Iran-US conflict began.

articles.title: Twisha Sharma death: Madhya Pradesh government proposes to transfer case to CBI - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Madhya Pradesh government proposed transferring the dowry death case of Twisha Sharma to the CBI. The notification, issued by Home Department Secretary Krishnaveni Desavatu, cites the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act for extending investigative powers to the state.  The case, registered at Katara Hills Police Station, involves allegations of harassment and dowry-related deaths against her husband Samarth Singh and mother-in-law Giribala Singh.

articles.title: Amazon Uk Chief: ‘It’s not their fault’: Amazon UK boss says education system is failing young workers | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Amazon’s UK country manager, John Boumphrey, argued that the education system is failing to prepare young people for work, contributing to rising unemployment. He stated that businesses are struggling to recruit workers with the necessary skills despite a million young people being out of education, employment or training. Boumphrey called for work experience placements to become compulsory and closer cooperation between businesses, local authorities and further education colleges to address regional skills shortages.  He emphasized that Amazon is facing difficulty recruiting enough workers for technical and engineering roles due to automation and robotics expansion in its warehouses.

articles.title: US deepens European uncertainty with deployment of 5,000 troops to Poland | NATO News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump announced the deployment of an additional 5,000 troops to Poland, citing his friendship with Polish President Karol Nawrocki. This move comes after a previous planned deployment was scrapped and deepens uncertainty surrounding the Trump administration's approach to NATO allies. European partners are left unsure about which areas they should prioritize for defense strategies in light of this erratic policy shift.  The Pentagon has also announced plans to reduce combat brigades in Europe, raising concerns among European allies.

articles.title: FO says PM Shehbaz to visit China from May 23-26 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif will visit China from May 23-26 to commemorate the 75th anniversary of diplomatic ties. During his trip, he will meet with President Xi Jinping and Prime Minister Li Qiang, and hold discussions on political, economic, and strategic cooperation. The visit is expected to strengthen the Pakistan-China all-weather strategic partnership. Tahir Andrabi, spokesperson for the Foreign Office, also addressed India's rejection of a supplemental award by the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) over the Indus Water Treaty, stating that it holds no political or legal value and will not invalidate lawful proceedings.  Andrabi called on the international community to hold India accountable for human rights abuses in occupied Kashmir.

articles.title: Rubio doubtful of diplomacy with Cuba as Trump renews threat of military action | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Marco Rubio renewed the threat of military intervention in Cuba, citing national security concerns.  Rubio, a strong critic of Cuba's socialist government, stated that while the administration prefers peaceful resolution, the likelihood of success is low given the current Cuban leadership. The recent indictment of former Cuban leader Raúl Castro on charges related to civilian plane shootings has fueled speculation about potential military action. Trump has previously threatened such intervention and imposed sanctions on Cuba, citing its ties with adversaries like China and Russia.  The US government's actions have been met with condemnation from countries like China.

articles.title: US navy chief says $14bn arms sale to Taiwan paused due to Iran war
articles.rephrased_article: US Navy Secretary Hung Cao announced a pause in a $14 billion arms sale to Taiwan, citing the need for sufficient weapons for the Iran war.  Cao stated that the pause is temporary and will allow the administration to ensure adequate munitions are available. The sale, which includes air defense missiles from Lockheed Martin, has been pending approval from President Donald Trump, who has expressed a willingness to use it as a negotiating tool with China.

articles.title: Turkish court ousts leader of main opposition party | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A Turkish court overturned the 2023 leadership election of the main opposition Republican People’s Party (CHP), reinstating former chair Kemal Kilicdaroglu as interim leader. The ruling is seen as a move against the CHP, which won a significant victory over President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's AK Party in the 2024 local elections and has been rising in polls. The CHP rejected the decision as an "attempted coup," while the government claimed it renewed faith in the rule of law.  The ruling sparked market turmoil, with the Borsa Istanbul index dropping 6 percent and government bonds sliding.

articles.title: LIC shares jump 5% after Q4 results, first-ever bonus issue. Here's what brokerages say - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: LIC, the state-run insurance company, reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 23,467 crore for the fourth quarter of FY26, marking a 23% year-on-year increase. The firm's net premium income rose 12% YoY to Rs 1.65 lakh crore. Citi and Bernstein have issued positive ratings on LIC shares, with Citi predicting an upside potential of over 84% and Bernstein a potential of more than 12%. JM Financial also maintains a "Buy" rating on LIC shares, raising its target price to Rs 960 apiece.  LIC's share price jumped 5% on Friday.

articles.title: What else does U.S. have in store for India’s foreign policy? asks Congress - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio
articles.rephrased_article: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh questioned U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio's future plans for Indian foreign policy, citing Rubio's recent announcements regarding a Venezuelan presidential visit to India and the postponement of the event due to an Ebola outbreak in Africa.  Ramesh expressed concern over Rubio's repeated pre-emptive pronouncements on India's foreign policy decisions, including the halt of Operation Sindoor.

articles.title: Donald Trump: 'If I do attend, I get killed': Donald Trump says he 'has a thing called Iran' stopping him from attending son's wedding - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump suggested he may skip his eldest son Donald Trump Jr.'s wedding in the Bahamas due to escalating tensions with Iran.  Trump stated that attending would likely result in negative media attention and potential harm, while not attending could also lead to criticism. The wedding is a private ceremony with only close family members and friends invited.

articles.title: US ‘hopeful’ as Islamabad tries to prevail on Tehran - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Marco Rubio expressed optimism for progress towards ending the war with Iran, despite rigid stances from both countries. Mohsin Naqvi, Pakistan's Interior Minister, is visiting Iran for a second time in a week to prevent communication breakdowns and facilitate talks between Iranian officials and US representatives. Reports suggest that Asim Munir, Chief of Defence Forces, may travel to Tehran if the talks lead to a breakthrough. While Iran has received the latest US proposal, the future status of the Strait of Hormuz remains a key sticking point in negotiations.

articles.title: Taliban ‘legitimising child marriage’ with new edict, activists warn | Child marriage | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Taliban have reportedly codified new laws that appear to legalize child marriage in Afghanistan, raising concerns from human rights groups and activists. The new legislation makes it nearly impossible for girls to seek divorce against their husbands' will, according to activists, who say the ban on education for girls has led to a surge in forced marriages.  The UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) expressed concern over the law, stating it represents another step in eroding Afghan women and girls' rights. The Taliban have dismissed criticism of their new legislation, claiming that those protesting are hostile to Islam and its foundations.

articles.title: Alberta to hold referendum on whether to remain in Canada
articles.rephrased_article: Alberta will hold a referendum on October 19th to determine whether the province should remain in Canada or pursue a second binding vote on separation. Premier Danielle Smith announced this decision, citing pressure from a restive independence movement and concerns about federal government policies that she believes infringe on provincial jurisdiction. The referendum question will ask Albertans if they want the province to remain part of Canada or begin legal proceedings for a separate referendum.  Smith supports remaining in Canada but acknowledges the concerns of those who advocate for separation, which is fueled by anger over resource development and perceived unfair treatment from Ottawa.

articles.title: Malaysia orders TikTok to address ‘defamatory’ content about king | Social Media | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Malaysia’s Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has ordered TikTok to address “offensive and defamatory” content about the country's monarchy. The watchdog issued this order after finding TikTok's response to previous notifications unsatisfactory and requiring the social media platform to strengthen its moderation policies and provide a formal explanation for failing to block "grossly offensive, false, menacing and insulting" content.  The MCMC stressed that it takes a serious view of online platforms disseminating false or detrimental content, especially regarding the monarchy.

articles.title: Nykaa shares rally 4%, hit 52-week high after Q4. Here's what Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley are saying - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nykaa reported a 28% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 2,648 crore for the March quarter, driven by strong growth in its beauty and fashion businesses. The company's gross merchandise value (GMV) also rose 28% year-on-year to Rs 5,241 crore. Nykaa CEO Falguni Nayar highlighted the company's multi-engine growth platform, with Beauty and Fashion businesses doubling their GMV in the past three years. Analysts from Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, and Elara Securities maintained positive ratings on the stock, citing strong revenue growth, profitability, and AI-driven efficiency improvements.

articles.title: Congress leader Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan elected Kerala Speaker - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan, a senior Congress leader, was elected as the Speaker of the 16th Kerala Legislative Assembly on Friday (May 22, 2026). He won with 101 votes, defeating A.C. Moideen and B.B. Gopakumar.  The election took place after G. Sudhakaran, the previous Pro Tem Speaker, chose not to vote.  V.D. Satheesan, the Chief Minister, and Pinarayi Vijayan, the Leader of the Opposition, led Radhakrishnan to the Speaker's chair.

articles.title: Greek Philosopher Epicurus: Quote of the day by Greek philosopher Epicurus: “You don't develop courage by being happy in your relationships everyday. You develop it by…” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Epicurus, a Greek philosopher, believed that courage is not developed through easy times but rather through facing and overcoming difficult experiences.  His quote emphasizes that people often discover resilience and strength during challenging periods, even if they don't recognize these changes while they are happening. While happiness and comfort can be important aspects of life, Epicurus argued that true fulfillment comes from navigating uncertainty and hardship, which ultimately lead to personal growth and development.

articles.title: Babar, Naseem recalled as PCB announces 16-member squad for Australia ODIs - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) announced a 16-member squad for the upcoming three-match ODI series against Australia, scheduled from May 30 to June 4. The squad includes players like Shaheen Shah Afridi (captain) and Babar Azam, who were not part of the recent Bangladesh series.  The team will assemble in Islamabad on Friday and begin training on Saturday, with the Australian team arriving in Islamabad on Saturday as well.

articles.title: Friday briefing: ​As Israel’s coalition collapses, can its prime minister hang on to power? | Israel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli legislators voted to dissolve parliament and call for new elections. The move is largely attributed to the current coalition government's instability, with opposition parties gaining traction in recent polls.  Benjamin Netanyahu, currently facing trial for corruption charges, remains a strong contender but faces an uncertain future as his political landscape shifts. Public opinion has shifted towards more progressive views, creating a complex and unpredictable race for power.

articles.title: Greenlanders protest against Trump outside new US consulate in Nuuk
articles.rephrased_article: Hundreds of Greenlanders protested against Donald Trump's ambition to control the island, gathering outside a new US consulate in Nuuk. The protest followed Jeff Landry, Trump's special envoy to Greenland, making his first visit and sparking diplomatic tensions.  Despite efforts to ease tensions, Greenlandic politicians largely boycotted events and Landry sparked unease by suggesting Greenland could become independent.  The US seeks a greater military presence in Greenland while the Greenlanders are adamant about maintaining their sovereignty.
